entries.headline: Fireblack walls get a new look

items.title: Fireblack walls' new look
items.text: Level 5 Fireblack walls have new art: smoked black glass in a thick stone frame, with magma swirling differently from block to block, a great black spike on top and four smaller ones at the corners.

entries.headline: Towers go higher: Sharpshooter and Blast Tower to level 10, the others to level 8

items.title: More tower levels
items.text: The Sharpshooter and the Blast Tower can now be upgraded to level 10, with the same costs, times and health as the overworld's Sniper and Cannon Towers at those levels. The Quake Tower, the Magma Tower, the Cinder Coil and the Obsidian Mortar go to level 8. Every new level needs Under Hall 6, and the biggest upgrades cost more than one yard's Resource Pods can hold, so you'll need the extra room your outposts give you. Outposts can upgrade their towers to the new levels too.

items.title: The Quake Tower's damage spread over 8 levels
items.text: A level 8 Quake Tower hits as hard as a level 6 one used to (5,500). The levels below were spread out along the same curve, so Quake Towers at levels 2 to 6 now hit less than before: level 6 does 3,844 instead of 5,500. Level 1 is unchanged.

entries.headline: The Monster Baiter comes to the Inferno; walls go to level 5, with Shiny upgrades to Studded Iron and Fireblack

items.title: The Monster Baiter comes to the Inferno
items.text: Build a Monster Baiter in your yard from Under Hall 4 and send monsters at your own defenses to test them. It can bait every overworld monster and every overworld champion at every level, every Inferno monster and champion you have unlocked (up to the level you have trained them to), and once you have finished Hell Freezes Over, Rimegrave and the ice cretins. Pick each monster's level on its card, choose the side they come from (or all sides, or anywhere), and have them arrive at once or in 2 or 3 waves, at normal or double speed. Practice raids, the default, put your yard back exactly as it was afterwards: nothing destroyed, nothing taken, nothing to repair. Real raids work like the old baiter. Each raid ends with a report of what was killed, what was destroyed and what they took, with Send again. You can save three waves to send again later.

items.title: Walls at levels 4 and 5
items.text: Blocks can now be upgraded past Forged Steel. Level 4, Studded Iron, has twice the health of level 3 and costs 250,000 bone and 250,000 coal (Under Hall 5). Level 5, Fireblack, has four times the health of level 3 and costs 1,000,000 bone, 1,000,000 coal and 500,000 magma (Under Hall 6); its magma swirls differently from block to block. Monsters choose their way round them exactly as they do round level 3 walls: only the health is different. Upgrade all walls offers the new levels too.

items.title: Upgrade every wall with Shiny to Studded Iron or Fireblack
items.text: The Store's wall upgrades now go to Studded Iron and Fireblack too, next to Granite and Forged Steel. Each wall's step to Studded Iron costs twice its step to Forged Steel, and its step to Fireblack twice that again; a wall that is already being upgraded isn't charged again for the step it's taking. Upgrading every wall, with Shiny or with resources, now works for every level. Fireblack blocks have a new look: black glass in a stone frame.

items.title: Monster info shows the new favorite targets
items.text: The line under each monster's name in the Strongbox, the Incubator, the ICS, the monster buttons and the Academy now matches how Valgos, Malphus, Grokus, Clinkerjaw and the Emberghoul choose their targets since the last update, instead of their old targets. It also shows Valgos's double damage to walls and half damage to storage, Grokus's half damage to defenses, and that Rezghul teleports. In the Academy, Rezghul's teleport and Malphus keeping out of the defenses' reach are listed with their abilities. Rezghul's description now names his favorite target the way the other overworld monsters' do.

items.title: Upgrade All (Resources) for walls offers every level
items.text: Upgrading all your walls with resources only gave you buttons for the two highest levels, so you couldn't take every wall to level 2 or 3 any more. It now opens its own window with a row for every level your walls can still go to, each showing how many walls it upgrades, the exact cost and its own button. A level your Under Hall or your resources don't allow yet says so, and its button is greyed out.

entries.headline: Monsters with new favourite targets, Rezghul teleports, heavy traps for champions, the Sulfur Bomb changed

items.title: New favourite targets
items.text: Valgos goes for walls and storage (Resource Pods, the Under Hall and outpost halls), whichever is nearest; it still does double damage to walls, and now half to storage. Malphus goes for harvesters and storage that no defense can reach first, then the rest, and walks round your defenses' reach when it can. Grokus goes for harvesters, storage and defenses, whichever is nearest, with half damage to defenses. Clinkerjaw goes for what its allies are attacking, or what is nearest them, up to 10 blocks away. The Emberghoul goes for anything, but once it's hurt it looks for something no defense can reach, up to 15 blocks away, and leaves what it was on for it. A block is the size of one wall block.

items.title: Rezghul teleports
items.text: Every 15 seconds, Rezghul can teleport up to 5 blocks along its way, as a powered-up Bolt blinks: it fades and can't be targeted while it moves, and it never passes a wall that stops its way.

items.title: Heavy traps
items.text: Heavy traps can be built: 6 in your main yard from Under Hall 4, and 2 in each outpost. Only a champion stepping on one sets it off, but its blast deals 25,000 damage to every monster near it.

items.title: The Sulfur Bomb's shield
items.text: The Sulfur Bomb's shield has changed. Small: no invulnerability, then 40% less damage fading over 15 seconds. Medium: invulnerable for 2 seconds, then 55% fading over 23 seconds. Large: 4 seconds, then 65% over 37 seconds. Huge: 6 seconds, then 80% over 44 seconds. The speed boost lasts the whole time.

entries.headline: The Devil's Contract: three bargains a day, a boon and a price

items.title: The Devil's Contract
items.text: Once a day at most (at least 23 hours apart), the Devil opens his ledger when you come into your main yard and offers three bargains. Pick one to read its terms and sign it in blood, or close the book to turn all three down. Every contract gives you a boon and asks a price, each for its own number of hours, both starting when you sign; once signed, it can't be broken. A contract is never offered alongside one you already have that touches the same thing, so they never stack. While one is in force, a red tag under your protection timer shows it and how long is left; click it for your contracts.

items.title: The ten bargains
items.text: Furnace Pact: bone and coal production +40% for 24 hours, but no sulfur or magma for 72 hours. Hoarder's Seal: storage +25% for 48 hours; when it ends, anything over 90% of your normal storage burns away. Merchant's Due: everything bought with resources 25% cheaper for 24 hours, but Shiny to finish things early costs 25% more. Second Shift: an extra worker for 24 hours (he stays until his last job is done), but no resource production at all for 24 hours. Bloodlust: your attacking monsters deal 10% more damage and take 15% more. Swift Horde: your attacking monsters are 15% faster with 20% less health. Thin the Ranks: monster housing +25%, but monsters cost 50% more to make, and any over your normal housing run off when it ends. Bone Bastion: your towers deal 20% more damage with 25% less range, against any attacker. Wrath Traps: your traps deal double damage for 48 hours, but re-arming them costs 50 times as much. Kitbinder: outpost kits 5% cheaper for 24 hours, but kits built then start with no damage protection. Champions are never affected.

entries.headline: Kit prices reworked; kits keep the outpost hall's calcification; outpost takeovers cost more; outpost layouts shared between your outposts

items.title: Kit prices: ready-made kits 1.8 times, your own kits 2 times
items.text: Every outpost kit is now priced the same way, from what is in it: what its buildings cost to build, upgrade and calcify, times 1.8 for a ready-made kit and times 2 for a kit you saved yourself, rounded down to a whole million. Bone and coal cost the same (the higher of the two) and sulfur half as much. Your own kits used to stop at about 716 million, however much was in them; that limit is gone, so a big saved kit costs what it is worth. Ready-made kits can still be bought with Shiny at the same prices; your own kits are paid in resources only, as before.

items.title: Kits keep the outpost hall's calcification, and ready-made kits can be calcified
items.text: Saving an outpost as a kit now also keeps how far its outpost hall is calcified, as it already did for its towers. Building the kit calcifies the hall that far, or leaves it as it is if it is calcified further already. The kit's price counts the hall's calcification, but when you build it over the outpost you are in, only the levels its hall doesn't have yet. Ready-made kits can now have calcified towers and a calcified hall too, and their prices count them. A kit you saved before 12 November has no calcification at all, and one saved before today none on the hall: save it again from a calcified outpost to include it.

items.title: Taking over a player's outpost costs more
items.text: Taking over another player's outpost now costs from 2.5 million up to 600 million of each resource, depending on the outpost's value, on a new scale that rises faster for bigger outposts. As a guide, an outpost built from each ready-made kit costs about: Ember 2.5 million, Brimstone 5.25 million, Demon 14.75 million, Damnation 73.5 million, Underlord 166 million, Apocalypse 600 million. The discount next to your home yard, the Conquest power-up and the extra cost in the Depths apply on top, as before. Taking over with Shiny and taking over tribe outposts cost the same as before.

items.title: Outpost layouts shared between your outposts
items.text: In an outpost, the Yard Planner's 10 layout slots are now shared by all your outposts: a layout saved in one outpost can be loaded in any other. There, your buildings take its places by kind, each going to the nearest place for its kind; what the outpost has no building for is left out, and the planner tells you how many moved. Look the plan over, then Apply it. The first time you open them, the shared slots get the layouts your outposts had saved, the newest first (up to 10). Your main yard keeps its own 10 slots.

entries.headline: Calcification: rings of bone that protect your towers, Resource Pods and Under Hall; kits keep calcification; new prices for the ready-made kits; the bone rings centred on the building's base

items.title: Calcification
items.text: Your defensive towers, Resource Pods and Under Hall can now be calcified: ringed with bone that takes the force out of every hit. There are four levels, and a calcified building takes 20%, 30%, 40% and then 50% less damage. Each level costs bone, coal and sulfur and a worker's time, and asks for Under Hall level 3, 4, 5 and 6. Press Calcify on the building. It does not work while it is being calcified, so a tower does not fire until the work is done. In outposts, towers and the outpost hall can be calcified too, and there every level asks only for the outpost's hall.

items.title: Kits keep calcification
items.text: Saving an outpost as a kit now keeps how far its towers are calcified, and building that kit calcifies them again. The kit's price counts it, the same way it counts each building's levels. Kits you saved before are unchanged. Building a kit over an outpost also leaves the outpost hall's calcification in place.

items.title: New prices for the six ready-made kits
items.text: The ready-made outpost kits are now priced from what is in them: twice what their buildings cost to build and upgrade, rounded down to a whole million. Bone and coal cost the same, and sulfur half as much, as before. Ember, Brimstone and Demon cost about what they did. Damnation, Underlord and Apocalypse cost more than before. The Shiny prices are the same.

later.note: now 1.8 times, and your own kits by the same rule

items.title: Bone rings in the right place
items.text: The bone rings of a calcified building sat a little high and off to one side. They are now centred on the building's base, where the old thorn rings sat. A building calcified a second, third or fourth time also kept showing its first ring until the game was reloaded; it now shows the new one straight away.

entries.headline: The Soul Crucible, a new building that turns one resource into another; monster synergies; two map fixes: renaming a bookmark, and a yard you just took over

items.title: The Soul Crucible
items.text: A new building for your main yard, on the Resources tab of the Buildings menu. Pour bone, coal, sulfur or magma you have too much of into its fire and take another of the four back. What comes back depends on the two resources and on the Crucible's level: bone into coal gives 25% at level 1 and 50% at level 6, bone into magma 40% and 80%. How much you can pour in a day is a share of your storage: 20% at level 1, up to 80% at level 6. Pick what to pour and what to take around the crucible, set the amount with the slider, and watch it go in and come out. When a resource is nearly full, a line at the top offers to pour it.

items.title: Monster synergies
items.text: Some monsters now fight better side by side. Spurtz and Zagnoid together each deal 12% more damage, and there are six more pairs: a monster's page in the Strongbox, and its tip when you pick an army, say which. You need about one partner for every two of the other, by housing, and they have to fight near each other. Champions have no synergies.

items.title: Renaming a bookmark
items.text: Renaming a bookmark in the map's side panel could stop the game with an error when the minute turned or the map updated while you were typing. The panel now waits until you finish, and what you have typed is kept.

items.title: A yard you just took over
items.text: With "Stay on the map" on, a yard taken over a few seconds after opening the map could go on showing as the tribe's for up to a minute, and pressing View on it stopped the game. The map now shows the yard as your outpost straight away.

entries.headline: Fewer, better big-win announcements; versus calls that leave chat; a fix for a black yard; outlines that move; shadows that don't stack; a smoother Balthazar; Korath's ground pound and monster animation fixes; richer champion skins, and four new ones; Balthazar can be juiced again; a live count on Watch; alliance power-ups and Store fixes

items.title: Fewer big-win announcements
items.text: Global chat now announces a Brimstone Pit win only when it pays at least 500 Shiny at 10 times the bet or more, and it beats that player's other wins from the last 24 hours, either in Shiny or in times the bet.

items.title: Versus calls leave chat
items.text: When a player looks for a versus partner, the call in global chat (with its Join button) is now removed as soon as they stop looking or find a partner, so old calls no longer sit in chat.

items.title: A fix for a black yard
items.text: On some computers, the yard was black with "Draw with the graphics card" on. The game now notices this and goes back to drawing the yard the old way on that computer. The graphics card also reads the pictures in a safer way now, which should stop monsters flickering in and out during big attacks.

items.title: Outlines on bomb targets
items.text: In an attack, buildings under a resource bomb's or siege weapon's ring now get the same white outline as buildings you point at in your own yard, instead of a tint on part of the building.

items.title: Outlines that move
items.text: The outline round a building you point at now moves with the building's animation.

items.title: Shadows that don't stack
items.text: Where two shadows overlap, the ground is now no darker than under one shadow.

items.title: Balthazar flies smoothly
items.text: Balthazar no longer jolts back and forth as he flies: his wingbeat now rises and falls smoothly instead of snapping back to the start of each beat. His wings also keep beating when he flies straight left or right, where they used to freeze.

items.title: Korath's ground pound
items.text: Korath's stomp (every third blow from level 5) now plays his ground pound: he rears up and slams the ground, and the stomp hits as his fists come down. Before, the stomp hit with no animation, with or without a skin.

items.title: Spurtz always show
items.text: A Spurtz facing up and to the right no longer disappears, in battle or in the compound.

items.title: Walks that keep walking
items.text: Monsters heading in some exact directions (Malphus and the Spurtz, among others) froze on one frame while they walked. Their walk now always plays.

items.title: Healed monsters stay visible
items.text: A monster healed back to full health vanished until its picture next changed: a standing Rimegrave, Ashkarr or ice monster could stay invisible, and in big battles healed monsters flickered. Now only its health bar goes away.

items.title: Korath's strike, every frame
items.text: Korath's level 3 champion no longer blinks out for one frame of his strike.

items.title: Richer champion skins
items.text: The champion skins Molten, Void, Gilded and Venom used to paint each champion in a handful of flat colours, with some parts left unchanged. Now every colour on the champion changes, and each skin has as much light, dark and colour variety as the champion's own look.

items.title: Four new champion skins
items.text: Every champion has four more skins in the D.A.V.E. Club's Champions tab: Crimson (blood red), Abyss (deep sea teal) and Storm (steel blue) for 200 Shiny each, and Solid Gold, a polished gold statue come alive, for 600 Shiny. Like the others, they're yours for good once bought.

items.title: Bone's old look
items.text: The Bone skin is back to its old look: pale bone with its glow, as it was before today's skin changes.

items.title: Balthazar can be juiced again
items.text: Balthazar sent to the Juicer now flies to it and is juiced. Since he was brought closer to the ground, he hovered where he was and never set off. Every other monster and champion was checked and goes to the Juicer as it should.

items.title: A live count on Watch
items.text: The Watch button on the top bar now shows a red circle with how many things are live right now (attacks, Brimstone Pit and Arcade games). It updates by itself and goes away when nothing is live.

items.title: Armament defends again
items.text: The Armament power-up now really gives your towers and blocks 50% more hit points and your booby traps 25% more damage. Before, it didn't reach your buildings at all, and it never helped against players attacking you. It now works against wild monsters and players alike, including on buildings you put down while it runs.

items.title: Conquest takes 25% off Shiny takeovers too
items.text: With Conquest running, taking over an outpost with Shiny now costs a quarter less too, not just when you pay with resources.

items.title: Housing Expansion works
items.text: Housing Expansion now really gives your Monster Bunkers 25% more room for 24 hours. It added no room before. Once it runs out, you can buy it again straight away.

items.title: Buy protection again
items.text: You can now buy protection again whenever you like, adding its time on top of any you have left. Once bought, it used to show as already owned until its time was up, even after attacking someone had taken the protection away.

entries.headline: Chat that comes back by itself; windows that fit a phone screen; store text that fits its card; fairer battle wins; safer monster transfers

items.title: Chat that comes back by itself
items.text: Sometimes, after the server restarted, chat stayed on "Chat had a hiccup" for everyone until the next restart. Chat now keeps trying to reconnect until it works, and the channels people joined in the meantime come back with it.

items.title: Every chat line shows
items.text: A line the game added in an older way (such as a list of the players you're ignoring) could land in the chat's history without being shown, which also threw off the scrolling. These lines now show like any other message from the game.

items.title: Windows fit a phone screen
items.text: On a phone held sideways, a tall window (such as the kits window with its page buttons) could open with its top and close button above the screen. It now opens lower, so its top shows.

items.title: Kits window easier to read
items.text: The kits window's note that kits are built instantly is now dark text instead of bright blue on brown.

items.title: Store text fits its card
items.text: A long description in the Store (Short Hop's, and some in French, Spanish and Portuguese) was cut off at the bottom of its card. It is now drawn a little smaller so all of it shows.

items.title: Fairer battle wins
items.text: A battle counts as won for the quest book (and toward the Basilisk) only if it knocked down at least one building and lasted at least 15 seconds. Attacking a yard that is already in ruins no longer counts as another win, and only a yard's real buildings count toward Buildings destroyed.

items.title: Safer monster transfers
items.text: Two monster transfers sent at the same moment (from two windows, say) could both move the same monsters. Now the second one waits for the first, and if the monsters have already gone it asks you to open the map again.

items.title: Your yard stays guarded
items.text: When a player attacks your yard and the server can't track the attack live, you can't build or save in that yard until the attack ends. Before, both games could save over each other.

items.title: Trick or Treat before it starts
items.text: Before Trick or Treat opens, its window says when the doors open instead of "over for this year", and the Mini-Pumpkins at the end are now added to your storage in the same step as the note that you got them, so they can't go missing.

items.title: Watch Live when nothing's on
items.text: With nothing live, Watch Live no longer says "0 things live now".

items.title: Outposts list summary fits
items.text: The summary under the Outposts list (what your outposts make, and which ones haven't been opened yet) ran past the window's right edge. It is now drawn a little smaller so it fits.

items.title: A guide to the map on your first visit
items.text: The first time you open the map, it now shows the Inferno's own guide to the map (the same pages as the map's ? button) instead of an old introduction with pictures from the overworld and a note about Flinger range that didn't apply to a new player. It shows once.

items.title: Welcome card with its picture
items.text: The Welcome to the Inferno card a new player first sees, and the While you were away card, had an empty picture box. They now show a picture.

items.title: Quest Book's back button stays clear of your Shiny
items.text: When the Quest Book's Go there opened a tall window like the build menu, its "◀ Quest Book" button sat in the top bar over your Shiny count. It now sits just below the bar.

items.title: Dots back in titles
items.text: Titles and buttons in the game's heading font dropped the middle dot used between parts, so the sign-in page read "Inferno Map Room 2  a custom server". The dot now shows, and so do other symbols that font lacks, such as French and Spanish « » quotes.

items.title: Œil de l'Abîme named in full
items.text: In French, the Eye of the Abyss decoration showed as "il de l'Abîme" in the build menu, because the menu's font has no Œ. It is now written "Oeil de l'Abîme".

items.title: Wart Bloom news in your language
items.text: The chat's Wart Bloom announcements (when one starts and when it ends) were always in English. They are now in French, Spanish or Portuguese when you play in that language.

items.title: More chat news in your language
items.text: The Brimstone Pit's big wins and jackpots, players looking for rivals at the Devil's Arcade, Moloch's Gauntlet being conquered and the Trick or Treat news in chat are now in French, Spanish or Portuguese when you play in that language. Names of players and games stay as they are.

items.title: Store cards fit in every language
items.text: In Portuguese and Spanish, several Store cards (the protections, Compound Expansion, Tower Overdrive) were cut off at the bottom, and their cooldown read like "1Dia 0hora 0minuto". The text is now drawn smaller where needed so it fits, and the cooldown is short, such as "1d".

entries.headline: Champion Statues: pick level 4, 5 or 6 and drawn properly; store items in the right tabs; a Decorations tab in the D.A.V.E. Club; Short Hop onto your own outposts; buttons kept inside the map windows, the attack result and the kits window; no extra box when viewing a yard; the newest pictures always shown, never old saved copies

items.title: Champion Statue: pick its level
items.text: Champion Statues of Korath, Drull and Rimegrave can show them at level 4, 5 or 6: pick the champion, then its level (the statue's Champion button, or the D.A.V.E. Club's Decorations tab). Ashkarr and the Basilisk have one look.

items.title: Champion Statues drawn properly
items.text: Your champion turns about its own middle on the turntable, the way it turns in a fight, and steps cleanly from facing to facing instead of showing two half see-through facings at once. The Basilisk statue shows the Basilisk, not a red lump, and the bronze reads as cast metal rather than a speckled pattern.

items.title: Store items in the right tabs
items.text: The Store's Extras tab is gone: each item is in the tab it belongs to. Construction has the Apprentice and Short Hop, Resources the Harvest Drone, Speed-Ups the Repair Crew, Training Manual and Academy Scholarship, Combat the Scout Report, Raid Insurance and Outpost Guard, and Looks the Champion Statue (beside the animated decorations) and the pets' Golden Coat, Name Tag and Treats. Buy still offers Gift beside it.

items.title: Decorations tab
items.text: The D.A.V.E. Club's Signs and Trophies tabs are one Decorations tab: the Sign, your Champion Statue (what it shows, and Champion to change it) and the event trophies, with Place in yard for those you've won.

items.title: Short Hop onto your own outposts
items.text: Short Hop no longer moves your main yard onto any wild monster yard. It swaps your main yard with one of your own outposts up to 10 cells away: your yard goes where the outpost was and the outpost goes where your yard was, and you keep both. Click your outpost on the map, then Short Hop here.

items.title: Map buttons inside their windows
items.text: Share this place in chat, Short Hop, Guard, Scout and the loot line now sit inside a map window's frame instead of under it, and the window grows to fit them. A player's name with its alliance no longer runs over the Location line.

items.title: No second box when viewing a yard
items.text: Looking at another player's yard no longer flashes a second box with Return Home under the yard's card for a moment: the card has those buttons from the start.

items.title: End of an attack: buttons inside, labels clickable
items.text: After an attack, Take over, Attack again, Back to the map, Home, Watch replay, Share and Brag all sit inside the result's frame, which grows to fit them. A click on the main button's label now works: the hidden please-wait line on top of it was catching the click.

items.title: Kits: pages inside the window
items.text: The kits window shows Page 1 of 4 with a button for each page, plus Prev and Next, inside its frame at the top instead of above it.

items.title: Pictures always up to date
items.text: Some pictures could stay old after they were replaced, such as the store and power-up icons and the Champion Statue, even after a forced reload. Each picture is now fetched by a name that changes whenever the picture does, so your browser and the site's network always get the newest one. Pictures that haven't changed still load from your browser, so the game opens just as fast.

entries.headline: Alliance power-ups: two new ones, Tier II and planned starts; the Store's Extras and three new store items; an easier Change Log; more frame rate limits, smoother and sharper drawing, Balthazar lower and round walls to decoys, pets drawn whole, and fixes for shadows, outposts, kits, watching, replays and chat

items.title: New power-up: Harvest Moon
items.text: A new alliance power-up: for 12 hours, every member's harvesters make 25% more bone, coal, sulfur and magma. It doesn't add to Production Overdrive: the stronger of the two applies. Like the others it recharges in 4 days, and hours can be bought off its charge for 5 Shiny each.

items.title: New power-up: Builders' Guild
items.text: A new alliance power-up: for 12 hours, every member's builds and upgrades take 15% less time. It recharges in 4 days, and hours can be bought off its charge for 5 Shiny each. The Power-Ups tab now fits all five.

items.title: Power-ups at Tier II
items.text: Starting a power-up now asks which tier: Tier I as before, or Tier II, which runs half as long again (18 hours instead of 12) but then takes 6 days to charge instead of 4.

items.title: Plan a power-up's start
items.text: The leader (or an officer allowed to start power-ups) can plan when one starts, from 5 minutes to 7 days ahead, and at which tier: press Plan start on its row and pick a time. It has to be charged by then. The alliance's chat says when it's planned, again 15 minutes before, and when it starts. Cancel plan takes it back.

items.title: Extras in the Store
items.text: The Store has a new tab, Extras: ten new things to buy with Shiny, described below. Their prices are set and charged by the server.

later.note: each item is now in the Store tab it belongs to; the Extras tab is gone

items.title: Harvest Drone
items.text: 120 Shiny: for 7 days, your main yard's harvesters bank themselves into storage, including everything they made while you were away.

items.title: Training Manual and Academy Scholarship
items.text: 150 Shiny each: for 7 days, Strongbox unlocks (the Training Manual) or Academy training (the Academy Scholarship) go 25% faster. One already under way speeds up too.

items.title: Raid Insurance
items.text: 60 Shiny: if you're raided in the next 24 hours, half of what that raid takes comes straight back to you, and you're told how much the next time you open your yard. It covers one raid, never more than was taken.

items.title: Short Hop
items.text: 75 Shiny: move your main yard onto a wild monster yard up to 10 cells away, from the map ("Short Hop here"). Your outposts stay where they are. As with any move, it's a day before the next.

later.note: it now swaps your main yard with one of your own outposts

items.title: Outpost Guard
items.text: 30 Shiny: protect one of your outposts for 12 hours, from the map ("Guard" on your outpost), on top of any protection it has.

items.title: Golden Coat, Name Tag and Pet Treats
items.text: From a pet's menu: a Golden Coat (400 Shiny) makes the pet gleaming gold for good; a Name Tag (25 Shiny) shows a named pet's name on a coloured tag, recoloured any time for free; Pet Treats (10 Shiny) have all your pets doing tricks and the zoomies by themselves for 24 hours, for visitors to see too.

items.title: Champion Statue
items.text: A new animated decoration, 750 Shiny: one of your champions in bronze, turning slowly on a plinth of glowing runes. Pick which of your unlocked champions it shows from the statue's Champion button. It's first among the animated decorations.

items.title: Gift Wrap
items.text: Anything in the Store's Extras can be bought for a member of your alliance, at the same price: press Gift and pick who it's for. They're told who it's from when they next open their yard; things they use later wait for them.

items.title: Apprentice
items.text: 100 Shiny, in the Store's Construction tab: one more worker in your yard for 3 days. When the time's up it finishes the job it's on first, then goes home. One at a time, and a week from one's start to the next. It can't be sacrificed.

items.title: Repair Crew
items.text: 90 Shiny, in the Store's Speed-Ups tab: for 7 days, everything damaged in your yards is repaired at once after a raid.

items.title: Scout Report
items.text: 10 Shiny, from the map: press Scout on another player's yard or outpost to see its towers by level, its traps by kind (not where they are) and its last 3 defences. Looking at the same yard again that day is free. It's listed in the Store's Combat tab.

items.title: The Store's tabs
items.text: The Store's six tabs line up: the Extras tab no longer sits over the window's edge or runs into its scroll bar.

items.title: Champion Statue turns smoothly
items.text: The champion on a Champion Statue now stays standing in the middle of its turntable as it turns (it used to shift about with a weapon or a tail), and turns smoothly and more slowly instead of jumping from one way to the next. A small champion is shown a little bigger.

later.note: it now steps cleanly from facing to facing, without the see-through blends

items.title: New pictures for the store's extras and the new power-ups
items.text: Every item in the Store's Extras, and the Apprentice, Repair Crew and Scout Report, has a new, more detailed picture in the style of the Store's other Inferno items, with an hourglass on the ones that last a while. Harvest Moon and Builders' Guild have new icons in the style of the other power-ups: your harvesters under a harvest moon, and an upgrade under way with two golden hammers.

items.title: An easier Change Log
items.text: The Change Log opens on what's new for you: only the changes you haven't seen yet (the top bar counts those, not days). Recent shows the latest week and Everything shows every day folded, so a click on a day opens it. Pick a topic (Yard & buildings, Monsters & battles, Map & outposts, Hellgate & Depths, Events & games, Alliances & chat, Screens & sign-in, Fixes) to see only that, each with how many changes it has. Titles only shows one line per change and a click shows what it means. New changes say NEW, your topic and Titles only are remembered, and on a phone the text and buttons are bigger. The Change Log page (/changes) does the same and fits a phone: the choices stay at the top as you scroll, and a link keeps them (Open as a page in the game opens it with your topic).

items.title: More frame rate limits
items.text: The page's "Frame rate limit" now also has 100, 180, 200, 280 and 360 fps, to match more screens (a 180 Hz monitor, say). A limit typed into the page's address that isn't a number is now ignored instead of turning the limit off.

items.title: Smooth again after turning off graphics card drawing
items.text: After the graphics card's drawing was switched off, the yard went on redrawing everything every frame. It now redraws only what changed again.

items.title: Small moves always shown
items.text: With the graphics card drawing the yard, a monster moving by a pixel or a slow fade could be missed for a moment and look stuck, then jump. Every small change now shows.

items.title: No black past the yard's edge
items.text: Dragging the view past the edge of the yard no longer shows black there while the graphics card draws it.

items.title: Less memory after changing yards
items.text: The pictures of the yard you left are now let go from the graphics card at once, instead of staying until the card had drawn for a while.

items.title: Smoother yards with cobwebs
items.text: With the Halloween cobwebs, buildings standing close together with no room for a web between them are now worked out once, not again on every frame.

items.title: Sharper monsters on phones
items.text: On phones and tablets, monsters drawn by the graphics card no longer show a sliver of the next frame at their edge or wobble by a pixel when zoomed in.

items.title: No pop-in on fast drags
items.text: Dragging quickly across a big battle no longer shows monsters popping in at the edge of the screen.

items.title: Basilisk moves between buildings smoothly
items.text: When a Basilisk lets go of a large building and wraps straight around the next one, he no longer snaps back to his usual length in an instant (his tail jumped). He now changes length gradually as he wraps.

items.title: Balthazar flies lower
items.text: Balthazar now flies a third as high as before, close over the ground, and bobs a third as much. He is still a flier.

items.title: Pets drawn whole
items.text: Pets are no longer cut off when facing some ways, such as a large Valgos facing left. Every pet is now drawn whole, whichever way it faces.

items.title: Balthazar walks round walls to a decoy
items.text: Balthazar now goes round walls to reach a decoy too, instead of flying straight over them.

items.title: Fewer path searches
items.text: When buildings fall, a hunting monster now looks for its next way once, instead of asking again for every way it was waiting for.

items.title: Monster Bunker shadows
items.text: A damaged level 1 Monster Bunker showed the shadow of a destroyed one, and a destroyed one had none. Both now show the right shadow.

items.title: Goo Factory pictures
items.text: The Goo Factory's pictures in its upgrade window were missing in outposts.

items.title: Each kit paid for once
items.text: A kit's payment now counts only for the kit and outpost it was made for. Sending the same build again (after a lost answer) is still never charged twice.

items.title: No spending the same Shiny twice
items.text: Spending Shiny in two places at the same moment (a pet and a purchase in your yard, say) could let both go through on one balance. The second is now refused: "You do not have enough Shiny for that."

items.title: Yards not locked past an attack
items.text: An attack on your yard can no longer keep you from saving it for longer than an attack can last (7 minutes), even if the attacker's game keeps sending its recording.

items.title: A full chat doesn't pause the game
items.text: When chat was full, the game took it for the server restarting and held your saves and attacks for a moment, again and again. It no longer does.

items.title: Watching shows a clean picture
items.text: When someone watches your game, the picture sent to them no longer keeps bits of an earlier frame where nothing was drawn.

items.title: Background work recovers when a thread fails
items.text: If the browser stops one of the game's background threads, the game now takes the work back at once: someone watching you no longer sees your game stand still for good, buildings still get their shadows and cobwebs, and monsters no longer pause for half a second before finding their way.

items.title: Steadier watching
items.text: A game watched by someone on a slow connection no longer makes everyone else watching it get a whole new picture twice a second, and a game sending pictures faster than the game ever does can no longer use up the server's watching for everybody.

items.title: Appearing offline hides your attacks
items.text: While you appear offline, nobody but you and the player you attack can watch your attack as it happens, including someone who had already opened it.

items.title: Replays: no extra Spurtz, no early fights
items.text: In replays, Spurtz Cannons no longer spawn real Spurtz that chase the replay's monsters (they piled up each time you moved through the replay), and moving back in a replay no longer shows monsters fighting before they were hurt.

items.title: A building without pictures
items.text: A building the yard has no pictures for no longer causes an error every moment (which could slow the game).

items.title: No blank screen on a slow load
items.text: When a yard's load had to be tried again, the "please wait" went away before the yard was ready, leaving a blank screen for up to a few seconds. It now stays until the yard appears.

entries.headline: Faster yards, outposts, map and chat, much faster big battles, work moved to background threads, faster light and shadows, changes to Valgos, King Wormzer and Balthazar, and fixes for the game clock, the planner, takeovers and drawing

items.title: More of the game in the background
items.text: The game now does some of its heavy picture work on your device's other processor cores, so the game itself keeps running smoothly. When someone watches your game, the pictures sent to them are made in the background (your game used to slow down while it was watched). A yard's shadows and Halloween cobwebs are also made in the background, so loading a yard no longer makes the game stutter. Browsers that can't do this make them as before.

items.title: Yards load faster
items.text: Working out a yard's ground used to stop the game for about a second as the yard loaded (several seconds on a phone). It is now worked out on your device's other cores while the yard loads, so yards open sooner and without that pause. The ground looks exactly the same.

items.title: Monsters find their way in the background
items.text: In a battle, the monsters' routes to their targets are now worked out on another core. Busy battles run smoother, and monsters get moving again sooner after a building falls.

items.title: Smoother dragging with path estimates
items.text: With path estimates shown in the Yard Planner, dragging a building no longer stutters. The paths are worked out in the background and redrawn a moment later.

items.title: Big replies don't hold others up
items.text: The server now compresses big replies, such as the world map, a yard or a replay, on its background threads, so other players' requests are answered while it does.

items.title: Faster light and shadows
items.text: The yard's light and shadows take much less time to draw, above all in a busy yard full of walls and monsters, so the game runs smoother with them on. In a battle of more than 30 monsters, the monsters keep just their round shadows.

items.title: Softer shadows
items.text: Shadows are a lighter shade, so the yard underneath shows through them more.

items.title: Shadows when hovering or banking
items.text: Hovering over a building, or banking a harvester (the resources spurting up), no longer adds a stray second shadow in the wrong place.

items.title: No cobwebs on decorations
items.text: Decorations stay clean of Halloween cobwebs. Buildings still have theirs.

items.title: Game clock after a long time away
items.text: When the game came back after a long time in the background (a phone locked, a tab put away), its clock could run ahead of the real time once the yard reloaded, by about as long as it had been away. It now picks up from the server's time.

items.title: Planner error after closing mid-drag
items.text: Closing the yard planner while dragging a wall line, an area or the ruler could cause an error the next time you used the planner. It no longer does.

items.title: Taking over a yard twice
items.text: Pressing Use Resources again on a yard you had just taken over said it wasn't destroyed enough. It now says the yard is already yours.

items.title: Replay links right after loading
items.text: Opening the game from a replay's link could say your yard was still saving and not open the replay. It now waits for the save and then plays it.

items.title: The graphics card draws the yard
items.text: The yard is now drawn by your device's graphics card, which is much faster with hundreds of monsters on screen. It looks the same as before. Devices without a real graphics card keep drawing it the old way. In busy battles the yard is no longer checked for changes before every frame, which saves more time.

items.title: Graphics card setting
items.text: Settings has a new "Draw with the graphics card" box, on at first. Turn it off if the yard ever looks wrong.

items.title: Lighter monsters for big crowds
items.text: Each monster takes less work every game step, and works out which way it faces only when it is drawn. Monsters far off the screen aren't drawn until you scroll to them. In battles of hundreds of monsters, each monster's picture is updated every second, third or fourth frame in turn, while they still move and fight every frame as before.

items.title: Lighter light and shadows in huge battles
items.text: With 400 or more monsters in a battle, the moving shadows of flames, smoke and flags are redrawn a little less often, and working out the monsters' shadows takes far less time, leaving more for the battle itself.

items.title: No freeze when the chat history arrives
items.text: When the game starts, the chat's history used to be laid out again for every line that arrived, freezing the game for about half a second. Lines that arrive together are now laid out once.

items.title: The map opens faster
items.text: Opening the map from an outpost now builds its tiles once, right at that outpost; before, it built them all around your home yard first and then again at the outpost. Tinted map tiles are also coloured by your browser's own graphics instead of pixel by pixel, which is much faster on most devices.

items.title: Faster text everywhere
items.text: Text is now measured from remembered letter widths instead of measuring every letter again, so windows, chat lines, labels and numbers appear faster. Objects added to the screen are also only told about it when something is listening, which speeds up opening big windows such as the map.

items.title: Lighter splats and shadows
items.text: Splats left by monsters are drawn once for each look and then copied, and a building's new shadow is drawn into its old picture when the size is the same, so busy battles create far fewer new pictures.

items.title: The graphics card's picture goes straight to the screen
items.text: On devices with a real graphics card, the yard drawn by the card is now shown on the screen directly, under the game's interface, instead of being copied back into the game's own picture every frame. That copy made the card wait for the processor, so big battles and scrolling the yard are smoother. Devices without a graphics card, or with "Draw with the graphics card" off, work as before.

items.title: Valgos is faster
items.text: Valgos now moves 1.5 times as fast at every level (speed 3, up from 2).

items.title: King Wormzer's splash reaches half as far
items.text: When King Wormzer pops up from underground under a building, the splash damage he deals around him now reaches half as far as before (50, down from 100), so it hits fewer of the buildings nearby.

items.title: Balthazar no longer flies over walls
items.text: Balthazar still flies, so traps and the towers that can or can't hit him work as before, but walls now stop him. He finds his way round them, or breaks through, the way walking monsters do. His monster info now says "Stopped by walls".

items.title: No stray pixels round monsters
items.text: With "Draw with the graphics card" on, many monsters (Zagnoid, Malphus, Valgos, Balthazar, Grokus, Sabnox, King Wormzer and others) could show a stray pixel or a thin line of pixels at the edge of their picture as they moved: a sliver of the next frame of their animation, or of a frame too big for their picture. They're now drawn exactly as without the card, every frame of every animation.

items.title: No black bars when dragging quickly
items.text: Dragging the yard quickly could show a black bar along the side coming into view, when the graphics card draws the yard and frames are smoothed between the game's own ("Frame interpolation", on by itself on fast screens). The yard's picture is now worked out where it is shown, so it always fills the screen.

items.title: No blur when zoomed in
items.text: Zoomed in on the yard (and on sharp screens), pictures were smoothed and looked blurry. They now keep their pixels crisp when shown larger; zoomed out they're still smoothed, so nothing shimmers.

entries.headline: Trick or Treat is coming (30 October to 2 November), light, shadows and Halloween cobwebs in every yard, and monsters go round walls

items.title: Trick or Treat
items.text: From 30 October to 2 November (US Central time), a jack-o'-lantern button under Moloch's Gauntlet's opens five doors, one for each wild tribe: the Hellionnaires, the Kozmodeus, the Abaddonakki, the Beelzenauts and Moloch's horde. Knock once on each. Behind every door there's an even chance of a treat, 25 Shiny on the spot, or a trick: 1,000 level 6 Zagnoids appear all at once in a ring round your yard and attack. It's a real raid that takes real loot, but destroy every last Zagnoid and the 25 Shiny are yours after all. Face each trick before knocking on the next door.

items.title: Mini-Pumpkins for every trick-or-treater
items.text: When Trick or Treat is over, everyone who knocked on at least one door finds 6 Mini-Pumpkins in their storage (Buildings, Decorations) the next time they come home, with Place it now.

items.title: Tricks you can watch again
items.text: Each trick is recorded like any raid, so it has a replay in your Attack Log, and Global chat hears about every trick and every one beaten. The events calendar (/events) counts down to the doors opening.

items.title: Cobwebs for Halloween
items.text: From 20 October every yard grows spooky. Cobwebs are spun in the gaps of buildings and strung between neighbouring ones, with dusty roofs, spiders and a gathering gloom. There are more each day until Halloween on 31 October, and they clear away by 3 November. Webs never stretch to walls, decorations or traps.

items.title: Light and shadows
items.text: Every yard is now lit from the evening side. Everything standing in it casts its own shadow away from the light: buildings and decorations, every monster and champion, workers, and pets (which also get a soft shadow under their feet). Moving parts cast moving shadows too. For a faster game on a slow device, turn off Light and shadows in the game's settings, under Display (Battery saver turns it off too). That also turns off the Halloween cobwebs.

items.title: Monsters go round walls
items.text: Monsters walk twice as far round a wall as before rather than break through it, so a wall line is worth more and gets broken less.

items.title: 20 more walls
items.text: Every Under Hall level allows 20 more walls: 30, 70, 110, 180, 280 and 320.

items.title: Repair All is back
items.text: A damaged building's panel has Repair All again while every repair is already under way: it finishes them all at once (free when they're nearly done). While some haven't started, Repair all still starts them all for free.

items.title: No alert over incubators
items.text: Incubators no longer show the ! alert icon when they're idle.

items.title: Tidier top buttons
items.text: The Daily Reward, Moloch's Gauntlet and Trick or Treat buttons no longer have text under them, and the outposts counter has lost its two small arrows (its button opens the Outposts list, which has Previous and Next).

items.title: Counters read 10 and over
items.text: The Daily Reward's day counter, and the mail's, show the whole number: day 12 read as 1 before.

items.title: Resource tips on outposts
items.text: On an outpost, hovering a resource no longer says what the harvesters hold or to click to bank, since an outpost's harvesters can't be banked, and clicking the bar does nothing.

items.title: No Hellgate board
items.text: The Leaderboards window has three tabs: Outposts, Alliances and Gamblers.

items.title: Path estimates in the Yard Planner
items.text: Three new Yard Planner tools, Tower path, Loot path and Any path, put a ground monster anywhere on the plan and draw the route it would take: going for defences first, loot first (harvesters, Resource Pods, the Under Hall), or whatever is nearest. Each building it destroys is numbered and each wall it breaks is crossed out in red, worked out the way the game's monsters choose and walk, and the routes update as you change the plan. Shift-click removes one.

items.title: See where a wall line starts
items.text: With the Yard Planner's Walls tool, a wall under the pointer shows where a line will start: green if it fits, red if it's blocked.

items.title: Watching stays light
items.text: Watching someone play in the Watch menu can no longer take over the server's connection, however long it goes on. Someone watching on a slow connection gets fewer pictures instead of a backlog, and when many people are watching at once, the games being watched send fewer pictures a second so everyone else's game stays quick.

entries.headline: 60 fps by default, full speed on slow devices, faster battles and windows, and fights in replays

items.title: 60 fps, or no limit
items.text: The game is now drawn up to 60 times a second by default (60 FPS), smoothly timed to your screen, instead of 40. Settings has a new Frame rate limit, from 30 to 240 FPS, or No limit (every refresh of your screen). The game itself still updates 40 times a second, its ticks, whatever you choose: monsters, attacks, paths and timers aren't faster or slower; only how often it's drawn changes. It replaces the old Frame interpolation choice; Battery saver sets 40.

items.title: FPS and ticks
items.text: Show frame rate is now Show on screen: FPS (how many times a second the game is drawn), Ticks (how many times a second the game itself updates: 40), both, or off.

items.title: Full speed on slow devices
items.text: On a slow device the game no longer slows down just because drawing can't keep up: it keeps its 40 ticks a second and draws less often instead (at least 10 times a second). Attacks, monsters and timers ran slower there before.

items.title: Big battles at full speed
items.text: With 60 FPS or No limit, an attack with lots of monsters could run at about half speed, with fewer frames too. While a battle is that busy the game now draws at its own 40 ticks a second instead, as with a 40 limit, and goes back to your limit once it's lighter. Monsters and timers keep their speed.

items.title: Faster big battles
items.text: Big attacks run much better: monsters find their way faster, a monster that isn't moving or changing isn't drawn again, and the yard is only drawn for frames you actually see. With 160 monsters an attack keeps its full 40 ticks a second (it slowed to about 25) and is drawn twice as often; with 500 it runs three times as fast as before.

items.title: A smoother Pit
items.text: The Brimstone Pit's lobby and games are drawn much faster: the yard underneath isn't drawn where the Pit covers it, glowing lights and text are quicker to draw, and the Ascent's sky is drawn once whenever it changes instead of every frame. The lobby and most games now run at 50 FPS or more (about 30 before); the Derby and the Ascent are three times as smooth.

items.title: Faster windows
items.text: Windows such as Mail, the Store, Leaderboards and Alliances are smoother with the pointer moving over them: what a window covers isn't drawn, glows are blurred once instead of several times, and text only redraws the part that holds its letters.

items.title: Smoother chat
items.text: A busy chat scrolls at close to 60 FPS (under 40 before).

items.title: Smoother map dragging
items.text: Dragging the Map Room's map is smoother: about 45 FPS, up from 25.

items.title: Steadier 60 FPS
items.text: A short slow moment no longer holds the game at 40 FPS for many seconds: it goes back to 60 as soon as it can, and a slow screen refresh now and then isn't mistaken for a slow device. Busy moments, like Hellgate Defense at 2x, keep more of their frames.

items.title: Fights in replays
items.text: Replays, and attacks you watch as they happen, now show the fighting. The yard's towers turn and fire at the attacking monsters and champions, and a monster or champion standing by something it's hurting plays its attack, facing it. A recording keeps where everything was and how hurt it was, not who hit whom, so the fighting is worked out from that. It's a close picture, not an exact one: the health and damage shown are still what really happened.

items.title: No more timeouts for being away
items.text: The game no longer stops when you leave it alone: no "Still there?" after 9 minutes and no stop after 10, however long you're away. Coming back after more than 5 minutes (a locked phone, or a tab put away) no longer stops the game with a Reload button either: your yard is brought up to date by itself, with a "Welcome back!". Anywhere else, like an attack that ended while you were gone, the game reloads by itself, still signed in.

entries.headline: Watch attacks and games live, safer saves, fairer kits and scores

items.title: Watch attacks on your yard
items.text: Your yard can now be attacked while you play, and you watch it happen: the attack plays out over your yard as it goes, with who is attacking and how much is destroyed. Nothing in the yard can be done until it's over, but the Map Room is yours to open, and closing it takes you back to the attack. When it's over, Return home. If you're elsewhere (another yard, or the map) you're told, with Watch. Attacks on your outposts can be watched the same way.

items.title: Watch anyone, live
items.text: A new Watch button on the top bar, between the Attack Log and the Leaderboards, lists everything going on right now: who is attacking whom (tribes too), and who is playing in the Brimstone Pit, the Devil's Arcade or Hellgate Defense, with how long it has been going. Pick a name to follow that player: you watch whatever they're doing, and whatever they do next. Attacks play out over the yard as they happen, a few seconds behind. Games show the player's screen as sharp as they see it, up to 15 times a second, in a viewer as big as your screen allows. Watch all shows the attack that has been going the longest, then anything else that's live, and waits for the next thing when nothing is. Next skips to something else.

items.title: Attacks show in Watch
items.text: Players in the middle of an attack now show in the Watch list and can be followed. Their attacks were left off it, so only Brimstone Pit, Arcade and Hellgate games showed.

items.title: Lighter Watch
items.text: Watching a game now sends only the parts of the screen that changed since the last picture, with a whole picture now and then: about a quarter of the data while things move, and nothing at all while the screen is still, so it keeps up better on slow connections. Recordings of attacks are sent compressed too, at a fraction of their size.

items.title: Appear offline hides you from Watch
items.text: Appearing offline (Who's Online) now also keeps you off the Watch list, and nobody can watch what you're doing. Your choice is kept on your account, so it stays after you reload the game or the server restarts.

items.title: See who's watching you
items.text: While anyone watches you (your game, or an attack you're making), a small list at the top right of your screen shows who, updated as people start and stop watching. Players appearing offline aren't named, only counted.

items.title: A game left open stays light
items.text: Leaving the game open on your yard no longer makes it heavier by the minute. Every path your monsters, pets and workers took as they wandered was kept, a little over 10 MB a minute, until a building moved; now only the last few are, so a tab left open for hours is as quick as a new one.

items.title: Closed windows are let go
items.text: Mail, Buildings, the Quest Book, the Attack Log, the Leaderboards, the Brimstone Pit and the other windows are let go once you close them. They stayed in memory until the browser window changed size, one more each time you opened them, and Mail's and Buildings' page arrows kept running.

items.title: An attack's last save is sent again
items.text: If the connection drops just as an attack ends, its last save (the loot, the damage and your losses) is sent again as soon as it's back, and the attack ends as usual. Before, the attack was left on an empty field and its loot never arrived.

items.title: Fairer yards
items.text: Closed a few ways a tampered game could add resources or Shiny to a yard, and a way odd requests could tie up the server.

items.title: Moving with one outpost
items.text: Accepting an invite to another world with one outpost now warns that you'll lose your outpost, instead of "all 1 of your outpost".

items.title: Kits are paid as they're built
items.text: A kit's price is now taken as the kit is built, so a dropped connection can't charge you for a kit you didn't get, and "Try again" never charges twice. Building one kit on several outposts pays for each as it's built. If your resources changed since you opened the kit window, you're told what it needs now instead.

items.title: Moving monsters between yards
items.text: Moving monsters to another of your yards moves only the monsters housed there, and waits while either yard is under attack. A move made from a map that's out of date is turned down with a note to open the map again, instead of being written over newer counts.

items.title: Battle quests match your Attack Log
items.text: The Quest Book's battles won, loot and buildings destroyed are now counted from each attack's own log, so they agree with your Attack Log. Loot counts what you actually brought home.

items.title: Event waves take their time
items.text: A wave won in an event counts once the wave has had time to play out. A game that reported a win the moment a wave began no longer gets its reward.

items.title: Rewards aren't undone by a save
items.text: Shiny or resources you got while the game was saving (a daily reward, a Gauntlet stage, a quest, a pet returned) could be undone by that save, and a purchase made at the same moment could come back. Each save now adds only its own change to what you have at that moment.

items.title: One takeover at a time
items.text: Taking over two yards at the same moment could charge you once and leave one outpost out of your Outposts list. A takeover now waits for your last takeover or move to finish, and says so.

items.title: Fair takeovers
items.text: A destroyed outpost can be taken over by the player whose attack destroyed it, straight after. One you've just taken is safe under its protection instead of still showing as destroyed, and one whose protection has run out counts as repaired. A takeover asks for resources you have, and waits while the yard is being attacked.

items.title: Moving your yard
items.text: Moving your main yard onto one of your outposts costs what the window says, and waits while that outpost is being attacked. The free move is only for a yard that's been overrun with no alliance to help. Each outpost's reach now comes from its own Flinger.

items.title: Alliances at the same moment
items.text: Two invites accepted at once, a join and a leave at once, or a kick beside a promotion no longer leave a player in two alliances or an alliance without a leader: one goes through and the other says so. If a leader on their own leaves just as someone joins, the newcomer leads. A power-up can't be started twice.

items.title: Mail and chat
items.text: No letters while you're muted in chat, and a limit on letters sent in a short time. A letter's subject is plain text. A line deleted by a moderator disappears at once, and a player who has left an alliance can't go on writing in its chat.

items.title: Arcade scores checked
items.text: Live matches hold every score to what the game can really score, Valgos Golf's final round included. In Hellgate Versus only the monsters the shop sells can be sent, and in Co-op a partner's game can't end your run with a message. Solo runs check their second number too (rows, waves, metres, aces).

items.title: Fairer boards and quests
items.text: Staff and players in test mode are left off the game's leaderboards. Hellgate waves count as the game's own timing allows, and the Quest Book's spending and "everything full" quests check your yard.

items.title: Strongbox champions
items.text: Unlocking Korath, Drull, Ashkarr, Rezghul or the Basilisk at once costs what the Strongbox's button says, and an unlock finishes when its time is up. Overdrive, Reduce by 1 or 2 hours and Finish now all still count.

items.title: Siege results checked
items.text: A Siege attack's wreck and time are held to what an attack can really do, so the Daily board and Duels are decided by real attacks.

items.title: Hellforge perks kept
items.text: In Hellgate Defense 2, a perk bought or taken back just as a run ends no longer loses the run's embers or the perk.

items.title: No catapults, really
items.text: A catapult fired in Moloch's Gauntlet counts against the "no catapults" trophy even if the game's report of the shot gets lost.

items.title: Raids on you
items.text: Attacks on me lists a wild raid once a day at most, and what it says you lost is never more than your yard can hold.

items.title: Invites from another world
items.text: If accepting an invite from another world fails partway, nothing happens: you stay where you were and keep what you'd have paid.

items.title: Signing in from a link
items.text: Opening the game from a sign-in link no longer leaves your login in the address bar or your browser history. Reloading the tab still keeps you signed in.

items.title: Chat for everyone
items.text: A flood of half-open chat connections can no longer lock other players out of chat, and an automatic ban now also stops the player's chat.

items.title: Store, skins and daily reward
items.text: Buying in an outpost costs the same rising price as in your main yard. A skin bought while you change your looks is kept, and the daily reward is always paid with the day it marks.

items.title: Small fixes
items.text: The Planner's Undo won't put a building on top of another. Auto play stops before going past "stop when down by". Selling a Hellgate tower asks again if its price fell while you decided. A second replay no longer plays on into empty time. "Reconnecting…" gives up after a minute, as it should. A save sent again after its answer was lost counts once. In Fusebug Blast, the other monsters no longer hop forward on a bumpy connection.

items.title: Map with a wrecked Map Room
items.text: The map opens even when an attack has wrecked your Map Room.

entries.headline: One kit on several outposts, fixed

items.title: One kit on several outposts, fixed
items.text: Choosing a kit for several outposts from the Outposts list (Select, then Choose kit...) works again from your main yard: the list had just closed without opening the kit window. The kit replaces whatever the outposts had, and you pay its price once for each outpost.

entries.headline: The game in your language, Brag in chat, streak savers, a player guide page and rules

items.title: Forgot your password?
items.text: Ask an admin on Discord: they can give you a one-time link (good for 24 hours) that opens a page where you choose a new password. Setting it signs you out everywhere else.

items.title: Signed-in browsers
items.text: Settings > Account > Signed-in browsers lists where your account is signed in (the game you're playing and the browsers that remember your name), with this one marked. Sign one out, or all the others at once.

items.title: Officers can do more
items.text: A leader can let officers start power-ups, mark other alliances as foe, neutral or ally, and edit the description (Overview, "Officers can also", Change). Until a switch is on, officers see those buttons greyed, and a click says why.

items.title: Kicked members come back as members
items.text: A player removed from an alliance who rejoins within 24 hours keeps their join date but comes back as a plain member. Leaving on your own and returning within a day still gives your role back.

items.title: Streak savers
items.text: Daily rewards have streak savers: every 14 days in a row earns one (you hold at most one), and it forgives a single missed day. If your streak breaks anyway, you can buy it back for Shiny on the day it broke, priced by its length, or start again.

items.title: Brag
items.text: Brag posts your win to chat ("I just wrecked Bob's yard: 87% and 1.2M looted") with the replay, or the yard on the map: on the attack log after a win, under an outpost or tribe-yard result, in a toast after a takeover, and in the Attack Logs' Replay menu.

items.title: Talk trash
items.text: From Attacks on me in the Attack Logs, post a taunt at whoever attacked you, with their replay. It goes to the chat tab you're on, at most once every 30 seconds, and nothing is sent while chat is off or you're muted.

items.title: The player guide is a page
items.text: "What's different?" and the game's guide links open the player guide as a web page: every chapter on one page with contents, a link to each part and a print layout. It's up to date and corrected (quests, Pit games, leaderboards, champions' housing, saved logins...).

items.title: Rules
items.text: A short Rules page (/rules) says how we play together: accounts and alts, invites, no bots or macros, chat, moderators, and how to appeal. It's linked from the guide, the help pages and the login page; type /rules in chat to open it.

items.title: Sharp when zoomed in
items.text: Zoomed in, the yard is drawn at your screen's own resolution (up to twice the detail), so the ground, buildings and effects look smooth instead of blocky, most of all on phones. With Battery saver on, it's drawn the lighter way, as before.

items.title: More of the game in your language
items.text: The Brimstone Pit, the Devil's Arcade and Siege, Hellgate Defense 1 and 2, pets and the workers' jokes, Moloch's Gauntlet, the Yard Planner, chat's replies and /help, the Outposts list, the D.A.V.E. Club, the login form, the page's settings and many messages are now in French, Spanish and Portuguese. Game and monster names stay as they are.

items.title: D.A.V.E. Club button
items.text: The small "Club" caption under the D.A.V.E. CLUB button is gone: the picture already says it.

items.title: Login error points to Discord
items.text: A wrong password now says to ask an admin on Discord for a reset link.

items.title: The Under Hall at every level
items.text: The Under Hall is rebuilt as an infernal machine that grows with every level: a little rusty boiler on clawed legs at level 1, then rings, red pipes, side stacks, thorns and a gold cage, up to level 6's caged lava core. Fire and smoke pour from its stacks (the core pulses at 6), and its damaged and wrecked states, build menu and quest pictures are all new.

items.title: Champion skins in battle
items.text: Your champions wear the skins you chose in the D.A.V.E. Club when they attack: on players' yards, on tribes' yards and at the Gauntlet's gates. Before, only champions defending a yard showed them. Replays show them too, for anyone watching.

items.title: Tidier attack and visit screens
items.text: In another player's yard, Return Home (or Open Map, Attack and Home, when you came from the map) is now in the player card with Bookmark, Share and the others, instead of in its own small white box. In attacks, End Attack is a full-size button in a matching dark panel. Long yard names fit their plate instead of running under the picture and the first resource, and a long attack timer stays on one line. The Flinger bar's text is easier to read.

items.title: Decorations, regrouped
items.text: The Decorations tab is now Animated (first), War, Yard, Trophies, Flags & Signs and Pets. The empty Nature tab is gone: its retired decorations show under Yard when you have some in storage. Won trophies and totems are with the other trophies, the Sign has moved to Flags & Signs, and the flags are in order by name.

items.title: Alliance Banner
items.text: A new decoration for 200 Shiny, first in Decorations > Flags & Signs: a crimson banner showing your alliance's shield, your own crest if your alliance has designed one. Everyone who visits or attacks your yard sees it, and it updates when your alliance's shield changes. Without an alliance it's a plain banner.

items.title: No slowdown from glowing monsters
items.text: Battles no longer slow down when your monsters glow from a Sulfur Bomb, a rage or Ashkarr's war cry. Each glow used to be redrawn for every monster in every frame, which took a battle from about 40 to under 30 frames a second. Now it's drawn once and shared, so glowing monsters cost the same as plain ones.

items.title: Server restarts, without the errors
items.text: When the server restarts, the game now tells you ("The server is restarting", with a countdown) and waits for it instead of failing: your saves, chat and map requests go through as soon as it's back (usually within a few seconds; it waits up to a minute).

items.title: Taking over wild yards
items.text: A wild monster yard opened twice at the same moment could be made twice, so a takeover after destroying it might fail with "failed unexpectedly". It's made once now, and a refused takeover says why (how destroyed the yard is out of the 90% needed, or that it's already yours), then the map shows the yard as it really is.

items.title: Monsters in their pen
items.text: Fixed an error that could stop the game while monsters paced in a pen that had moved or gone.

items.title: Tidier windows
items.text: A pass over the newest windows so nothing is cut off or crowded, in every language and on small screens: the Quest Book's daily quests show their whole task (and when new ones come, on your clock), the D.A.V.E. Club fits a small window and its emote names no longer run into each other, the Buildings sub-tabs are as wide as their names, the outposts counter's ◀ ▶ sit inside its bar, the Outposts list closes with its X like every other window, the alliance history says "2 weeks ago" in full, and the map's search box and Depths banner no longer cover anything.

items.title: One clock everywhere
items.text: The Wart Bloom, Moloch's Gauntlet and your workers' sacrifices now give times the same way as the rest of the game ("Monday 00:00", "1 Nov 2026, 01:00"), and Settings > Account > Signed-in browsers says "5 minutes ago".

items.title: Hell Freezes Over
items.text: [ CLASSIFIED ]

entries.headline: Find on the leaderboards, Collect all on the quest dock, and more fixes

items.title: When the server can't be reached
items.text: If logging in gets no answer, the game tries again by itself a few times before giving up, and then says it couldn't reach the server (or that you seem to be offline) instead of "an error occurred on the server".

items.title: Find a player
items.text: A Find button next to Find me: type a name, or part of one, and the leaderboard jumps to that player.

items.title: Collect all from the dock
items.text: When two or more quests are ready, the quest dock shows Collect all, so you don't have to open the Quest Book.

items.title: Zoom keeps your place
items.text: The zoom button no longer drops a building you're placing or moving, and zooming back in returns you to where you were.

items.title: Moving onto a blocked spot
items.text: Dropping a building you're moving where it can't go keeps it in your hand and says so, with Put it back, instead of snapping it back so you had to click Move again.

items.title: Who's Online filters
items.text: Who's Online has All, My alliance, Friendly and Hostile filters and a Find box for a name or alliance tag.

items.title: Attack Log details
items.text: The Loot column shows the main resource and how many others ("1.2M Bone +2") instead of one sum of different resources, and a report gives the exact day and time as well as how long ago.

items.title: Big numbers
items.text: From a billion, the resource bars show short numbers ("2.34B") instead of shrinking the digits; the bar's tip gives the exact amount.

items.title: Your language, remembered
items.text: The language you pick on the login page is kept for your next visit, and a first visit opens in your browser's language when the game has it (English, French, Spanish or Portuguese).

items.title: Faster loading
items.text: The game's texts are now sent compressed (about a quarter of the size) and kept by your browser between visits, and pictures are kept until they change instead of being rechecked every hour.

items.title: Lighter in the background
items.text: A game left in a background tab no longer wakes the computer 125 times a second when nothing is due.

items.title: Requirements you can click, fixed
items.text: Clicking an unmet requirement in the build or upgrade window now opens that building, as intended (it did nothing outside the tests).

items.title: The Strongbox says what it takes
items.text: Locked monsters in the Strongbox show the level and Sulfur they need ("Lv 2 · 38.4K Sulfur", red where you're short), or "Can start". The Strongbox opens on the next monster to unlock instead of Spurtz, and its upgrade says which monsters the next level unlocks.

items.title: Clearer Academy
items.text: The Academy says "Needs Academy level N" and still shows the training's cost and time, says what it's busy with and for how long, and its arrows skip monsters you can't train. Its upgrade says what level monsters it can then train to.

items.title: The Incubator explains itself
items.text: Clicking a locked monster in the Incubator says it isn't unlocked yet, with Open the Strongbox; not enough Magma says how much it costs and what you have, with Top up. Unlocked monsters are listed first, and the window shows the Compound's room (with what's queued).

items.title: What next, after a battle
items.text: The battle result now offers the next step: Take over now after flattening a tribe's yard or an outpost, Attack again after a failed attack, or Back to the map, with Home beside it. (The single button said Return Home but opened the map.)

items.title: Retreat is harder to hit by mistake
items.text: A champion's Retreat button no longer sits right against Send, and on a touch screen it is held for half a second; a tap says to hold it.

items.title: When the new day starts, on your clock
items.text: The Quest Book's daily page and the Siege's tries say when the new day begins in your own time ("at 19:00 your time"), since the day changes at midnight UTC.

items.title: Not enough Shiny
items.text: The not-enough-Shiny window says how many more you need and how many you have, lists what is ready to collect now (your Daily Reward, quests), and has a button that takes you there.

items.title: When a save doesn't go through
items.text: If the server stops answering, the game says "Not saved yet, trying again" from the second missed save, then shows Reconnecting… and carries on by itself once the server answers, instead of stopping with an error after the fifth.

items.title: Back from a yard you looked at
items.text: Looking at someone's yard, the panel has Home beside Open Map, and Open Map brings back that yard's window on the map (Attack, Message, …) instead of the bare map.

items.title: The button says it's working
items.text: While the server is asked, the button says "Logging in…" or "Creating account…", so a slow line doesn't look like a click that did nothing.

items.title: Easier to hit Collect
