items.text: On the quest dock, Collect takes a click over the whole height of its row and a little around the button; a near miss used to open the Quest Book.

items.title: Bigger tabs
items.text: The Global and Alliance tabs and Who's Online? take a click over the whole height of the chat's bar, not just their words.

items.title: The name menu on phones
items.text: On a touch screen the menu that opens on a name has taller rows, and there is a gap between Copy name and Ignore.

items.title: Moloch's Gauntlet: counting down
items.text: The Gauntlet's window counts down while it is open (by the second in the last hour), and its button's tip says when it opens or closes, in your own time.

items.title: A sound when work finishes
items.text: A short sound plays when a building or an upgrade finishes while you are in the yard (one sound when several finish together).

items.title: A refused attack is said on the map
items.text: Before an attack leaves the map, the game asks whether the yard can be attacked right now. If it can't (damage protection, someone else attacking it, its player online), you're told why there, instead of being sent home first and told there.

items.title: Which yards may lose protection
items.text: The "may lose damage protection" question names your yards it means, with their coordinates.

items.title: Back after being away
items.text: When the game has stopped because nobody was there, moving the mouse, pressing a key or coming back to the tab says "Welcome back! Reloading…" and reloads by itself.

items.title: Typos in your email
items.text: Creating an account with a misspelt common address ("gmial.com") asks whether you meant the right one, and the welcome reminds you which address you log in with.

items.title: Why the password is asked
items.text: When a saved login can't sign you in any more, the login page says why: it ran out after 14 days unused, or it was ended by a password change or a sign-out.

items.title: Forgetting a saved account
items.text: The × on a saved account is easier to hit, and closing one shows "Forgot … Undo" for a few seconds.

items.title: Switch account asks first
items.text: The Switch account button asks before signing you out.

items.title: Load asks about unsaved changes
items.text: Loading another plan while this one has changes that aren't saved asks first.

items.title: Power-ups ask first
items.text: Activating an alliance power-up asks first, saying how long it works and how long it then takes to charge again.

items.title: Moving your main yard onto an outpost
items.text: Moving your main yard onto one of your outposts asks a second time, with Keep as the safe answer, since the outpost and its buildings are destroyed.

items.title: What a purchase leaves
items.text: Shiny confirmations say how many you have and how many you'll have after.

items.title: Fewer Shiny questions, if you like
items.text: The page's settings (the gear) have "Ask before spending Shiny": Always, or only over 10, 50 or 200 Shiny.

items.title: Reduce motion
items.text: A Reduce motion setting turns off screen shakes, nodding buildings and zooming windows. By default it follows your system's own setting.

items.title: Music and effects volumes
items.text: Music and Effects have their own volume sliders in the page's settings, under the main Volume.

items.title: Windows open where you left them
items.text: The Store (from the bottom bar), the Alliance window and the kit window open on the tab or page you last had, until you reload.

items.title: Players' rows open their menu
items.text: Clicking a player on the leaderboards opens the same menu as a name in chat: send a message, jump to their yard, invite them, copy the name.

items.title: Your invites so far
items.text: The Invite Friends window says how many friends have joined through your link, how many earned the Shiny, and how many haven't played yet.

items.title: One window for several attackers
items.text: When two or more players attacked you while you were away, one window lists them all (how often and how long ago) with a button to the Attack Log, instead of one window each.

items.title: 3x speed and Pause
items.text: The speed button goes 1x, 2x, 3x, and a solo run has a Pause button (Go on to carry on). Co-op and versus runs keep time with the other player, so they have no Pause.

items.title: Leaving a game asks first
items.text: Pressing the Arcade's X during a game asks before leaving; a match against another player counts as a loss.

items.title: The lobby remembers its page
items.text: The Arcade opens on the page of games you last looked at, until you reload.

items.title: The Attack Log says when it's from
items.text: Under the list: "Refreshing…" while a new one is asked for, then "Updated 14:02" in your own time.

items.title: Who's Online says when something failed
items.text: If Appear offline (or online) doesn't go through, it says so, and a list that couldn't be refreshed says how old it is.

items.title: Bookmarks that didn't save
items.text: If saving your bookmarks fails, the game says so, with Try again; the change used to vanish at the next load.

items.title: Downloading a replay that's gone
items.text: Download first checks the replay is still on the server, and says so if it isn't, instead of opening a blank "not found" page.

items.title: Emotes: tap, then tap again
items.text: On a touch screen the first tap on an emote shows which one it is; a second tap sends it.

items.title: Taking monsters out of an Incubator's queue
items.text: On a touch screen a tap on a queued monster shows its remove X; a second tap takes one out. A touch used to take it out at once.

items.title: Bigger Pit chips
items.text: On a touch screen the Brimstone Pit's chips take a press a little outside them.

items.title: A report after a wild raid
items.text: The window after a wild monster raid says what it cost: buildings lost, walls broken, traps set off and the resources taken; if traps went off, Re-arm All is offered.

items.title: @all and @officers
items.text: In Alliance chat, a line from the leader or an officer with @all counts as a mention for every member (highlighted, and counted on the tab); @officers calls the officers. From anyone else it is an ordinary line.

items.title: Better Browse
items.text: Browse finds alliances by their tag as well as their name, shows the tag before each name, and shows members as "12/50" or Full.

items.title: Damage in the Outposts list
items.text: The Outposts list has a Damage column: "Attacked!" while an attack on the outpost is under way, its damage in red from 50%. Sorting by it puts outposts under attack first.

items.title: Next and Previous follow the list
items.text: Next and Previous outpost go through your outposts in the order the Outposts list was last sorted, instead of the order you took them.

items.title: Keys for the yard
items.text: In your yard: the arrows or W A S D move the view, + and - zoom, H goes to the Under Hall, B opens Buildings, P the Yard Planner, T the Store, M the map, Q the Quest Book and F full screen. Press ? for the list. They do nothing while you type or while a window is open.

items.title: Keys on the map
items.text: On the map: the arrows or W A S D move, + and - zoom, H goes home, B bookmarks the place in the middle, and F puts the cursor in Find.

items.title: Keys when attacking
items.text: In an attack: 1 to 9 put a monster from that row into the Flinger (hold Shift to fill it), Space flings where the pointer is, and Esc empties the Flinger when nothing else is open to close.

items.title: The guide from the Quest Book and the Change Log
items.text: The Quest Book and the Change Log link the "What's different?" guide, as the login page does. The Quest Book's "Old quest list" link is now called "The original game's quest list".

items.title: Chat remembers its tab
items.text: Chat opens on the tab you used last (Global or Alliance) in this browser.

items.title: "More..." is now "Info"
items.text: The building panel's "More..." button is called "Info", which is what it opens.

items.title: Cancelling an upgrade says what you get back
items.text: Cancelling an upgrade now says what comes back (its whole cost) and that the time already spent is lost, instead of only "This can not be undone".

items.title: The Flinger in numbers
items.text: The attack bar shows the Flinger's load in numbers ("Flinger 1,240 / 1,600") next to the percentage, and each monster's tip says how much Flinger space it takes.

items.title: The Gauntlet's result in numbers
items.text: After a Gauntlet attack, the window says how much of the gate you destroyed, how much breaks it, the attempts left and the prize still waiting.

items.title: Back to the Attack Log after a replay
items.text: Closing a replay you opened from the Attack Log takes you back to the log, scrolled where you were.

items.title: Jump to the quest a locked one needs
items.text: A locked quest's "Opens when you collect: ..." is a link to that quest.

items.title: Try again on the Change Log
items.text: If the Change Log can't be loaded, a Try again button loads it.

items.title: Place a trophy straight away
items.text: The message for a trophy you won has a Place it now button that puts the trophy in your hand.

items.title: Fewer popups
items.text: No more "Having fun? Invite a friend" popup after a few idle minutes, and no "Veni, Vidi, Vici!" Brag popup after taking over a yard. The Invite button in the top bar is still there.

items.title: Invites name who sent them
items.text: An alliance invite shows who sent it (the leader or an officer), instead of always the leader.

items.title: Revoking a move invite asks first
items.text: Revoking an invitation to move next to you asks before it's done.

items.title: Keys in Hellgate
items.text: In Hellgate Defense: Space starts the wave, F changes the speed, P pauses, Tab picks the next tower, Q W E R upgrade it and S sells it. Help lists them.

items.title: Selling an upgraded tower asks first
items.text: Selling a tower you have upgraded now asks first, with the gold you get back.

items.title: Pause in solo games
items.text: Press P or Esc to pause a solo game in the Devil's Arcade, and again to go on. Q quits from the pause. A solo game also pauses when you switch to another window or tab.

items.title: Keys in the Arcade's menus
items.text: In the Devil's Arcade the arrow keys turn the lobby's pages, Esc goes back from a game's page or a result, and Enter plays again from a result.

items.title: Keys in the Pit
items.text: In the Brimstone Pit, Space presses the game's main button (Deal, Start, Bet, Drop, Spin, Buy, Place bet, never Cash out). In Cinderjack H, S, D and P are Hit, Stand, Double and Split. In Higher or Lower the up and down arrows are Higher and Lower.

items.title: Housed and incubators in the Outposts list
items.text: The Outposts list shows how full each outpost's Compound is ("120/200", or "None" without one) and how many of its incubators are busy ("1/2"). Both columns can be sorted.

items.title: Outposts wasting resources
items.text: When a storage at home is full, the Outposts list says which and how much your outposts are wasting an hour.

items.title: Kits compared with your outpost
items.text: In the kit window, each kit's rows are green where it has more or higher than what the outpost has built, and red where it has less.

items.title: Night Owl is in your time
items.text: Night Owl now says it counts the hours in your own time.

items.title: Siege times with tenths
items.text: Siege's board shows times to a tenth of a second ("1:23.4"), so two close runs are told apart.

items.title: Several emotes in one line
items.text: Shift-click emotes in the picker to add several to your line (up to 5) before sending. A plain click still sends one at once. The emote button also has more room around it, so a near miss no longer presses Say.

items.title: The Gauntlet's Shiny this month
items.text: Moloch's Gauntlet shows this month's Shiny: claimed, still to win and lost. The text no longer runs into the gates after an attack.

items.title: A warning before the idle stop
items.text: A minute before the game stops for being idle, a soft chime and "Still there?" give you a chance to move. The stop itself chimes too.

items.title: Quieter repairs, louder cues
items.text: Repair all no longer plays twelve seconds of hammering. Collecting the daily reward and picking an ordinary wart make a sound. Hellgate's wave horn and the quest sound are louder.

items.title: Volume sliders with a %
items.text: The page's Volume, Music and Effects sliders show their % and follow your ears: half way sounds half as loud.

items.title: The login page
items.text: The login page leads with the game's name, "Inferno Map Room 2 · a custom server", and the saved accounts say they are kept in this browser for 14 days, up to 5 of them.

items.title: Mutes say why
items.text: If you are muted in chat, the game now tells you at once, for how long, and the reason when one was given.

items.title: Warnings before maintenance
items.text: When the server is going down for maintenance, players in the game are now warned 15, 5 and 1 minutes ahead. When it begins your yard is saved and you are told, with a button to reload.

items.title: Search the Change Log
items.text: The Change Log has a search box, and clicking a change's area tag (Yard, Map, Chat...) shows only that area. Click the tag again to see everything.

items.title: Idle incubators stand out
items.text: An incubator with nothing queued, or one holding a hatched monster with no room for it, now shows the same alert mark as a full harvester.

items.title: When you can build more
items.text: In the build menu, a building at its limit says when the Under Hall lets you build more, for example "+1 at Under Hall 5".

items.title: Transfer all monsters
items.text: The monster transfer window has an All button (then None), and Shift-clicking + or - moves every monster of that kind at once.

items.title: Shiny left in the Quest Book
items.text: The Quest Book's top line says how much Shiny you can still earn from its quests and chests.

items.title: Sort by any column
items.text: Click a leaderboard heading to sort by it (biggest first, or A to Z for names). Click again for the other way, and a third time, or on #, for the normal order. Ranks stay the same.

items.title: Change your password
items.text: The page's settings (the gear at the top right) have an Account part with Change password: type your current password and the new one twice. Your other devices and saved logins are signed out; the game you are in goes on. Password managers can fill the fields.

items.title: Handing over keeps you an officer
items.text: A leader who makes someone else the leader now stays on as an officer instead of becoming a plain member.

items.title: Power-up notices
items.text: The alliance chat now says when one of your power-ups runs out, and when one is charged again and ready to start.

items.title: When the game can't start
items.text: If the game can't reach the server as it starts, it now shows Try again, says when you appear to be offline (and tries again by itself when you are back online), and has a link to copy the details for a bug report. The old link to another project's Discord is gone.

items.title: No lost last save
items.text: Closing the tab, or putting the game away on a phone, right after doing something no longer loses it: the waiting save is sent at once.

items.title: Repeated attacks grouped
items.text: In the Attack Log, the same attack over and over in a row (the same tribe yard, say) is now one line, "Name ×6" with the best damage and the loot added up. Click the name to see each attack.

items.title: See an upgrade before buying
items.text: Point at a tower's upgrade button and its stats line shows what changes, for example "Damage 250 → 350".

items.title: Full refund before the wave
items.text: A tower sold before the next wave starts gives back everything you paid for it since the last wave, so a misplaced tower costs nothing. After a wave it sells at 70% as before.

items.title: Keep the building in your hand
items.text: Opening the Quest Book or the Store while placing a new building no longer drops it: it is put out of sight and is back in your hand when the window closes.

items.title: Inferno tips
items.text: While a yard loads, a tip about the Inferno shows under the loading box. The old "Pro Tip!" popups from the original game (Facebook, buying workers) are gone.

items.title: Where you were signed out from
items.text: If you are signed out because your account started playing somewhere else, the game now says on which browser and at what time, and how to change your password if it wasn't you.

items.title: Invite links
items.text: A friend's invite code is taken off the address once the game has kept it, so reloading or switching account doesn't tie a second account to it, and it is forgotten after 30 days.

items.title: Announcements once per account
items.text: An announcement from the admins is now shown once to each account, on whichever device it is seen first, and not again on your other devices. Every account used in the same browser still sees it.

items.title: Rules as you sign up
items.text: The sign-up form shows the rules for the name (2 to 12 letters, numbers or _) and the password (8 or more characters with a symbol) under the fields, each ticked once it is met.

items.title: Already playing: keys and a warning
items.text: When the account is already playing somewhere, Enter now chooses Play here and Esc chooses No, and the question warns when the other one may be another tab of this same browser, whose unsaved changes would be lost.

items.title: A tidier Change Log
items.text: The Change Log now lists only what players can see or use: the admins' own tools are no longer in it, and every change is filed under one of a fixed set of areas, each with its own colour.

items.title: Passwords up to 72 characters
items.text: New passwords can be at most 72 characters long. Longer ones were accepted before, but only their first 72 characters counted, and very long ones could never log in.

items.title: More in /help
items.text: Chat's /help now also lists /changes (the Change Log), /guide (the player guide), Appear offline in Who's Online and the emote button.

items.title: Who's Online for shared connections
items.text: Who's Online is now limited per player, so people playing from the same home or school connection no longer see it go stale together. Alliance pins and the D.A.V.E. Club have their own limits too.

items.title: Warts during a Wart Bloom
items.text: The Wart Bloom chip now says how many warts are in your yard, and warns when it is full, since a full yard wastes the bloom's growth.

items.title: Mute stays muted
items.text: The sound and music buttons now remember your choice in this browser wherever you press them (in an attack too), without saving the yard each time. Music turned back on plays the Inferno's own track at your Music volume.

items.title: Help pages
items.text: Three new pages: questions and answers (/faq), when things happen and in which time zone (/schedule), and how Shiny is earned and what it costs (/shiny), always up to date with the server's settings. In chat, type /faq, /schedule or /shiny to open them.

items.title: What's different? is in English
items.text: In French, Spanish and Portuguese the login page's "What's different?" button now says that the guide it opens is in English.

items.title: The top bar while visiting
items.text: Visiting another player's yard now keeps Alliances, the Attack Log, the Leaderboards and the Change Log in the top bar. The quest dock says that the Quest Book opens in your own yard, instead of doing nothing.

items.title: Raid warning: level and time
items.text: The wild monster alert now says the raid's level and when it arrives, in your own time and in how long.

items.title: Gauntlet's last day
items.text: On the last day of Moloch's Gauntlet, the game reminds you once that it closes soon and how many gates are still to beat, with a button to it.

items.title: Interface clicks switch
items.text: The page's settings (the gear) have an Interface clicks switch: off, the buttons and windows stop clicking while the game's other sounds play on.

items.title: No music behind errors
items.text: The music stops when the "Oops" window appears, instead of looping on behind it (the battle track too).

items.title: Sounds for lives and defeat
items.text: Losing a life in Hellgate Defense has a sound of its own, and losing the run plays the Hall falling instead of the "building placed" sound.

items.title: A sting at the end
items.text: Every Devil's Arcade game now ends with a short sound, a fanfare when you win. Before, only a new best made one, and only once the server had answered.

items.title: Wins and losses sound right
items.text: In the Brimstone Pit a win now sounds louder than a loss (it was the other way round), big wins and jackpots get a fanfare, and a lost bet makes a dull thud instead of the error buzz.

items.title: A sting after a defence
items.text: When a raid on your yard ends, a short sound says whether you held it off or it broke through.

items.title: Music picks up where it was
items.text: After an attack, a wave or a Hellgate run, the yard's music now goes on from where it was instead of starting over, and it loops without the short gap it had every minute.

items.title: Music in big battles
items.text: Two of the game's sound channels are now kept for the music, so a huge attack can no longer stop the music for good, and sounds asked for before your first click no longer all play at once when you click.

items.title: Notification sounds
items.text: The page's settings (the gear) have a new switch, off unless you turn it on: a short sound when someone mentions you in chat, a letter arrives or a quest is ready to collect.

items.title: A sting after your attacks
items.text: When one of your attacks ends, a short fanfare plays for a win and a crash for a loss.

items.title: Replays you can hear
items.text: Replays now play the battle music and you hear buildings being hit and wrecked. Before, they were almost silent and played the yard's music.

items.title: MAX and dimmed chips
items.text: Bet chips you can't afford are dimmed, and a new MAX button bets the most you can afford. In Roulette and the Derby it counts what is already on your slip.

items.title: Asked before a big bet
items.text: A bet of 100 Shiny or more that is over half your Shiny asks you first. Say Yes once and that game won't ask again until you reload.

items.title: Rules at a click
items.text: Magma Drop, Roulette, Bone Pile, Ascent, Dice and the Derby have a ? button by LOBBY with their rules and pays.

items.title: Today's totals
items.text: The History tab shows what you have bet, been paid and won or lost today (the Pit's day, which turns at midnight UTC).

items.title: Cinderjack hint
items.text: Turn on HINT in Cinderjack to see the basic-strategy move (Hit, Stand or Double) for your hand. It's off until you turn it on, and it remembers your choice.

items.title: Sound switch in the Pit and Arcade
items.text: The Brimstone Pit and the Devil's Arcade have a speaker button that turns the game's sound off and on.

items.title: Your place on the board
items.text: After a game, the result shows your place on that game's leaderboard and how far you moved up ("#7 (up 3)"). Matches ranked by wins also show your wins and losses.

items.title: Leave after you're knocked out
items.text: Knocked out in Lava Floor, Bone Brawl or Fusebug Blast while the match goes on? You can keep watching, or press LEAVE to go back.

items.title: Hellgate Defense 2 run summary
items.text: The end of a Hellgate Defense 2 run shows the waves you held, the towers still standing and your MVP tower, with a Hellforge button to spend your embers straight away.

items.title: Siege rematch
items.text: A finished Siege duel has a REMATCH button that challenges the same player again.

items.title: Better bet history
items.text: The History tab has a game filter, pages, and an OLDER button for the bets before. Click a bet to see its details: what you bet, what it paid and how the round went.

items.title: QUICK mode
items.text: Magma Drop, Roulette, Magma Slots, Korath's Fortune and Scratchers have a QUICK button that shortens the animation. Each game remembers your choice.

items.title: Bet on the next round
items.text: In Ascent and Devil's Dice you can bet while a round is running: the bet is queued for the next one. Click it to cancel.

items.title: Past races
items.text: The Derby has a PAST RACES button with the last races' winners, their odds and who came second.

items.title: Tidier numbers
items.text: Multipliers are written the same way everywhere (1.40×, 60×), and the bet field shows thousands separators (1,250).

items.title: Rename and delete planner slots
items.text: Yard Planner slots can be renamed and deleted, and names can be up to 30 characters. Empty slots are greyed out in Load.

items.title: Current yard in the planner
items.text: Load has a Current yard button that resets your plan to the yard as it is now.

items.title: Coloured range circles
items.text: In the planner, ground, air and trap ranges have their own colours and a legend, and hovering a building shows its own range.

items.title: Planner grid, nudging and ruler
items.text: The planner has a grid that also snaps buildings to their neighbours' edges, and the arrow keys move the selection one cell at a time. A ruler measures distances in cells.

items.title: Walls tool shortcuts
items.text: In the planner's walls tool, Shift-drag puts walls back in storage and Alt-drag lays a box. The tool shows how many walls you have left.

items.title: Sent invites
items.text: Leaders and officers can see the alliance's sent invites (who, when and by whom) and cancel them from the Recruit tab. Invites now run out after 14 days.

items.title: Browse keeps its rows
items.text: Pages you looked at in the last minute come back at once. If a page can't be loaded, the last list stays with a "Couldn't refresh" note instead of going blank.

items.title: Members search and Joined
items.text: The Members tab has a search box and a Joined column, and members not seen for over a week are marked inactive.

items.title: Keep or renew pins
items.text: The leader can keep a board pin for good, and officers can renew one for another 30 days. The top pin also shows above the Alliance chat tab.

items.title: Hell Freezes Over
items.text: [ CLASSIFIED ]

items.title: Track up to 3 quests
items.text: Pick up to 3 quests in the Quest Book to keep in the dock. They come right after the ones ready to collect and are marked with a flag.

items.title: A free daily reroll
items.text: Once a day you can swap one of your daily quests for another. "Hold off the wild" is only given when a raid can still come before the day ends.

items.title: More Go there buttons
items.text: Quests about warts, towers, harvesters, mail, decorations, kits and your alliance now have a Go there button.

items.title: Put up a Sign
items.text: A new optional quest: put up a Sign in your yard.

items.title: Attack Log filters and older attacks
items.text: The Attack Log shows the last 24 hours' attacks and loot, can be filtered by yard type and by won or lost, and loads older attacks past the first 60.

items.title: Target filters
items.text: The map's Filters panel has a Targets column: a level range, hide protected or locked yards, and only yards in your flinger's range. Yards left out are faded, or hidden if you prefer.

items.title: Back and Recent
items.text: The map has a Back button that returns to where you were before each jump, and a Recent list of the last 5 places you looked at.

items.title: Why Move is greyed
items.text: When you can't move your yard to an outpost (a Depths outpost, or the 24-hour wait), the greyed Move button says why and how long is left. Your own yard's popup has a Relocate button.

items.title: Outpost facts on the map
items.text: Your own outpost's map popup shows its production, monsters housed, idle workers, protection, towers and damage, with an Open + Kits button.

items.title: Towers and Needs attention
items.text: The Outposts list has a Towers column (count and lowest fortification, or Empty), and a "Needs attention only" switch that the list's and the top bar's arrows follow. Depths outposts next to a portal are marked in purple.

items.title: Two buttons on a first visit
items.text: The first time you open the game in a browser, you choose between Create account and I have an account.

items.title: Every sign-up problem at once
items.text: If your name is taken and your email already has an account, both are shown, each under its own field, with free names you can pick and a Log in instead link.

items.title: Invite links say who invited you
items.text: An invite link opens the sign-up form with the name of the player who invited you and the Shiny you both get.

items.title: Language and keyboard
items.text: Picking a language changes the form at once, and Tab now reaches your saved accounts and the Register or Login link too.

items.title: The sign-up note fits
items.text: The note under the sign-up form ("Your email doesn't have to be real...") is no longer cut off at the bottom.

items.title: Damage per second
items.text: The Strongbox, the Academy and the incubators show damage per second, worked out from how often a monster really hits, instead of a Time row that was the same for every monster.

items.title: What a monster goes for
items.text: Monster info shows a tag line: what it targets, whether it flies, burrows or jumps walls, and its reach or range. The attack bar's tips show health and damage per second too.

items.title: Countdowns over the Strongbox and Academy
items.text: An unlock or training in progress shows its countdown over the building.

items.title: Academy overview and abilities
items.text: The Academy has an Overview of every monster's level, whether it can train and how long the next level takes. Champions list the abilities they get at each level.

items.title: Juicer shortcuts
items.text: In the Juicer, Shift-click a monster to pick all of that kind and Ctrl-click (or Alt-click) to take one off. The window shows how much Magma you get back.

items.title: Planner: Apply asks first
items.text: Apply now tells you how many buildings will move and how many stay, and marks the movers on the plan while it asks. Apply selection moves only the buildings you selected.

items.title: Planner: coverage map
items.text: A Coverage tile shades the ground by how many towers reach it and outlines buildings no tower covers.

items.title: Planner: tidier bar and slot counts
items.text: The bottom bar is Save, Load, then Clear, with Apply on its own at the right. Save and Load rows count each layout's buildings and how many aren't in this yard.

items.title: Planner: Import moves fewer buildings
items.text: Import places each building on the nearest matching spot, so buildings already in place stay put.

items.title: Report a chat line
items.text: A player's name menu has "Report this line". The line and the ones around it go to the admins.

items.title: Emote shortcodes and recent emotes
items.text: Type :grin: (or any emote's name between colons) and it becomes the emote. The emote picker shows your recently used ones first.

items.title: Offline chip and online count
items.text: While you appear offline, an Offline chip shows by the chat tabs. When the chat is folded, its button says how many players are online.

items.title: One block list
items.text: Ignoring a player in chat also blocks their mail, and unignoring lets both through again. Reporting a letter now reaches the admins and also ignores the sender.

items.title: Mutes come with a reason
items.text: When you are muted, you see it and the reason at once.

items.title: An All button for the Flinger
items.text: Each monster in the attack bar has an All button to the right of "+" that puts every one of that kind in the Flinger. Once they're all in (or no more fit) it becomes None and takes them all out. Double-clicking "+" no longer fills the Flinger; Shift-click still does.

items.title: A seek bar
items.text: The replay player has a seek bar with the attack's damage drawn along it and marks where catapult shots landed. Click or drag it to jump to any moment.

items.title: Keep a replay
items.text: Press Keep on a replay to keep it for good, so it isn't cleared away with old replays. You can keep up to 10.

items.title: Replay links and better chat pills
items.text: Share can copy a link that opens the game straight into the replay. Replays shared in chat read "Ann vs Bob · 87%".

items.title: Long attacks recorded whole
items.text: Replay parts that couldn't be sent because the connection dropped are sent again. A very large attack's replay is marked "cut short" instead of quietly losing parts.

items.title: Events calendar
items.text: Type /events in chat to open a calendar of every event and daily reset: Moloch's Gauntlet, the monthly invasion, the Wart Bloom, daily quests and rewards, Moloch's Favor and the arcade dailies. It shows each one's state and countdown in your own time, with a Go button.

items.title: Undo a kick
items.text: After removing a member you have 5 minutes to undo it; they come back with their role and join date. The alliance feed says who removed whom.

items.title: Coming back within a day
items.text: A member who leaves or is removed and rejoins within 24 hours gets their role and join date back. The Leave question says what you would lose.

items.title: Recruit filters
items.text: The Recruit list can be filtered to your world, a minimum level and players active in the last day, and has pages.

items.title: Stances both ways
items.text: When another alliance changes its stance toward yours, your feed says so, and Browse shows how each alliance sees you.

items.title: Taking the lead
items.text: If the leader hasn't been seen for 14 days, the longest-serving active officer can take the lead from the Overview. It never happens by itself.

items.title: No lost results
items.text: A Hellgate run whose result couldn't be recorded is sent again by itself, and the end screens and Leave offer Try again. A result sent twice is only counted once.

items.title: Ask before selling, a weekly free reset
items.text: Selling an expensive tower at a loss asks first, and so does buying a Hellforge perk. Once a week you can reset your perks and get all their embers back.

items.title: Siege Daily tries given back
items.text: A Siege Daily try that never got going (a crash or a reload before any damage) is given back.

items.title: Reconnect in versus and races
items.text: If your connection drops in a versus or race game, you have 12 seconds to come back to the same match.

items.title: Join from chat
items.text: Players looking for a rival in any versus or race game are announced in chat, with a Join button.

items.title: Six kit slots
items.text: You can now save six of your own outpost kits instead of three, and rename or delete a saved kit from the kit window.

items.title: Name your outposts
items.text: Give each outpost a short name from the Outposts list (click its X, Y or Value). The name shows in the list, on the map and in the map's sidebar.

items.title: Abandon one outpost
items.text: An outpost of yours can now be let go on its own from its map popup, after typing ABANDON. The rest of your outposts stay.

items.title: Take over and stay on the map
items.text: Tick "Stay on the map" when taking over a yard to keep the map open for the next one.

items.title: Transfers by free space
items.text: When sending monsters, choose the target outpost from a list showing its free room; + and All stop at that room.

items.title: Outposts and Portals in the sidebar
items.text: The map's sidebar has an Outposts tab (each with Go) and a Portals tab listing both ends of each portal, plus a Depths button under Home.

items.title: Pick all warts
items.text: A wart button in the workers' column sends your idle workers to every wart in the yard, one after another, with one summary of the golden ones at the end.

items.title: Break all ice
items.text: While the curse's ice is in your yard, a button sends idle workers to every patch and sealed tower that can be worked.

items.title: Upgrade all walls, re-arm all traps
items.text: The build menu's Defensive tab has Upgrade all walls and Re-arm all traps buttons, each with its count.

items.title: Decorations several at a time
items.text: After placing a decoration from storage, the next one stays in your hand while more are stored (Esc stops). "Place all" on a stored decoration puts every one down next to the Under Hall.

items.title: Workers and pets can be clicked
items.text: The pointer becomes a hand over workers and pets, and new players see a "Click me!" over a worker for their first sessions.

items.title: Moloch gives a worker back
items.text: A sacrificed worker can be taken back within 2 minutes, as long as you still have the Shiny it earned.

items.title: Visiting a yard
items.text: Inside someone's yard a panel shows the owner (alliance, stance, coordinates, online or last seen; click for their menu), with Bookmark, Share, Open on map and Attack when in range. A click on a building shows its card: level, health, a tower's range and damage, a storage's rough loot.

items.title: Visit your mates' yards
items.text: Members has Visit yard; from there, step through the list's yards with the arrows and go Back to Members.

items.title: Signs and pets when visiting
items.text: Signs with a message are marked and show it on hover; clicking someone's pet shows its name and kind.

items.title: Loot estimate when scouting
items.text: A visited yard's panel shows roughly what destroying it all would give, and the map's popup for a yard you've looked at repeats it. During an attack the counters show taken / still lootable.

items.title: Watch or share right after an attack
items.text: The result of an attack on a player has Watch replay and Share in chat.

items.title: Which side a raid comes from
items.text: While a wild raid counts down, an arrow at the edge of the screen points to where it will land.

items.title: Catapult keys
items.text: Esc puts an aimed bomb away, Q aims the last one again, and a bomb already fired this attack says so.

items.title: Targets
items.text: A Targets button lists every yard within your reach (type, level, damage, protection, distance), sortable, with Go and Attack.

items.title: Damaged tribe yards marked
items.text: On the world map and the minimap, damaged tribe yards show orange and those ready to take over red (a Filters switch hides them).

items.title: Bookmarks with what's there now
items.text: Bookmarks show the owner or tribe, protection or damage, the distance and whether it's in reach; sort them, and give each a colour by clicking its pin.

items.title: A minimap of the Depths
items.text: In the Depths the minimap shows its 10×10 platforms, outposts, damaged camps and portals; click to go there.

items.title: A bigger map
items.text: On a big enough window the map room grows to fill it.

items.title: Copy a layout you visit
items.text: Copy layout on a visited yard's panel puts its buildings (no traps or decorations) in your Yard Planner's Import.

items.title: Planner: import from your layouts, share in chat
items.text: Import can take any of your saved slots, outposts' slots, kits, copied layouts or earlier versions. Export can share a layout in chat; its pill opens the planner with it.

items.title: Planner: compare and plan ahead
items.text: Compare shows another plan over yours with the differences marked. Plan ahead puts buildings you haven't built yet on the plan; when you build one, loading the plan puts it on its spot.

items.title: Earlier versions kept
items.text: A planner slot or kit saved over or deleted keeps its earlier version for 7 days, with Restore.

items.title: Better touch
items.text: Two fingers pan at normal size, a double tap zooms in and out, hover tips no longer stick after a tap, a tap just beside a small button finds it, and lists scroll with a finger.

items.title: Full screen and settings
items.text: One full-screen button works the same everywhere. In full screen on a computer a gear appears near the top, and F10 opens the settings anywhere (Esc closes them).

items.title: Touch controls everywhere
items.text: Arcade touch controls appear on any device once you touch the screen, and can be set left-handed, bigger or smaller, and more see-through.

items.title: Clearer errors
items.text: A failure the server reported now shows its reference in small print, so it can be looked up, and a window still loading says when the server can't be reached.

items.title: Popups in turn
items.text: Messages that come while your yard is loading wait their turn instead of piling up, and the Gauntlet and Siege windows open after the popups your yard brought.

items.title: One close button
items.text: Windows share one close button, the same size in the same corner, and a few windows have a "?" with a short how-to.

items.title: Windows fit small screens
items.text: The Quest Book, Leaderboards, Attack Log and Change Log shrink to fit a small window.

items.title: Back where you came from
items.text: A window or yard opened from the Quest Book or the Outposts list offers a way back to it.

items.title: The Alerts bell lists its alerts
items.text: The bell says what it holds (2 attacks · 1 battle report) and opens one list with View for each, or Show all.

items.title: Captions and long-press tips
items.text: The picture-only buttons have captions (Daily, Club, the Gauntlet's gate), and a long press on them shows their tip on touch screens.

items.title: Fold the quest dock
items.text: The quest dock folds down to its one-line summary and back.

items.title: Phones: easier windows
items.text: On phones the attack monster list has bigger buttons and more rows, the building panel has larger rows with Stop and Relocate last in red, incubators show a monster's stats on the first tap and add on the second, and Attack Log rows open on a tap with "…" for Replay and Jump.

items.title: Phones: placing buildings
items.text: On touch screens a building being placed sits above your finger, with ✓ and ✕ to place or cancel.

items.title: Bigger sign-in on phones
items.text: The sign-in form fills a phone held upright.

items.title: Trophies and Pets in the Club
items.text: The Club has a Trophies tab (what you've won, how to win the rest, Place in yard) and a Pets tab; a pet can be swapped for one that's out in one step.

items.title: Previews before you choose
items.text: A ground shows in your yard behind the Club at once (and goes back if you close without saving), and a champion skin shows walking before you buy it.

items.title: Give a pet back
items.text: A pet never fed can be returned for its full price within 10 minutes of buying it, or released later for half.

items.title: Looks in the Store
items.text: The Store's Looks tab leads to skins, emotes, alliance crests and animated decorations.

items.title: Trophies by names
items.text: Small trophy icons show next to players' names in the chat name menu and the Members list.

items.title: Welcome back
items.text: Logging in after attacks shows one Welcome back card instead of a chain of popups: who attacked which yard, the damage and loot lost (with Replay and Revenge), damaged buildings (Repair all), injured monsters (Heal all), full harvesters (Bank all), and rewards waiting.

items.title: Your outpost under attack
items.text: While you're online, an outpost attacked, wrecked or taken shows a notice (with the horn) and a badge on the Outposts button.

items.title: Siege duels: your turn
items.text: A Siege duel mails you when it's your turn, and duels show how long they have left.

items.title: Keep a yard's monsters at home
items.text: When attacking from the map, Yards lets you keep any of your yards' monsters at home.

items.title: Trackpads
items.text: On a trackpad, two fingers scroll the yard and a pinch zooms; a mouse wheel still zooms.

items.title: Press and hold to move
items.text: Hold a building for a moment to pick it up and move it, as the Move button does.

items.title: Drag a line of walls
items.text: With a wall in hand, drag on the yard to lay a straight line of them, each paid as it goes down (Shift-drag still scrolls).

items.title: Per 100 housing
items.text: A monster's page in the Strongbox says its health and damage per 100 housing, to compare monsters of different sizes.

items.title: Tower damage per second
items.text: Towers show their damage as per shot × shots a second = DPS, and their range in cells.

items.title: Refill army
items.text: The Compound remembers your last full army and Refill army queues what's missing in your incubators, telling you the Magma first.

items.title: Production of outposts not yet opened
items.text: The Outposts list works out what an outpost you haven't opened yet makes, marked as an estimate, instead of "?".

items.title: Take over and build a kit
items.text: The takeover window can build one of your kits on the new outpost right away, paid with resources, in the same step.

items.title: One kit on several outposts
items.text: Select in the Outposts list ticks outposts to build one kit on all of them, with the total price asked first.

items.title: The Gauntlet's gate in view
items.text: The Gauntlet's panel shows the army you'd attack with and a map of the gate's layout.

items.title: Wait for a match in the background
items.text: Waiting for a rival can go on in the background, with a chip at the top to come back or leave the queue.

items.title: Faster start
items.text: Sounds load after your yard (and not at all while muted), big siege sheets only when used, and the loading screen shows real progress and says when the connection is slow.

items.title: Battery saver and smoother frames
items.text: Settings have a Battery saver button, a switch for glow effects, an Auto setting that draws frames with the screen, and a hint to use the sharpest resolution on scaled displays.

items.title: Offline page
items.text: Opened from the home screen without a connection, the game shows a small page that retries by itself.

items.title: Sounds where they happen
items.text: Effects are levelled against the music, battle sounds come from their side of the screen and are quieter off-screen, and one sound plays at most four times at once.

items.title: Who can join
items.text: An alliance's leader sets who can join (open, by request or by invite only, and a lowest level), and Browse says it on each row.

items.title: Restore a disbanded alliance
items.text: An alliance you disband is kept for 14 days, and you can bring it back from the Alliance window, with you as its leader.

items.title: Friends you invite land near you
items.text: A friend who joins through your invite link gets their yard near yours, and an invite into your alliance if you lead it or are an officer.

items.title: Player card and View yard
items.text: A name's menu in chat starts with the player's card (level, world, outposts, ranks, best Hellgate Defense run, when they started) and has View yard, whatever world they're on.

items.title: Chat over reading windows
items.text: Chat stays usable while the Quest Book and other reading windows are open.

items.title: "Warn your friends" does something
items.text: The popups after training or unlocking a monster, a champion's return, a lab power-up or a siege weapon have buttons that act: Train next level, Hatch now, Share in chat.

items.title: Browser notifications
items.text: Turn on browser notifications in the page's settings to be told, while the tab is hidden, when it's your turn in a Siege duel, an outpost is attacked or an alliance invites you.

items.title: One way to say when
items.text: Times ago and dates read the same everywhere ("5 minutes ago", "6 months ago", one date format), and big numbers are grouped the way your language does it, negatives too.

items.title: Colour-blind colours
items.text: A colour-blind setting shows friends in blue and enemies in orange on the map and in chat.

items.title: Language and interface size
items.text: The page's settings pick the game's language (remembered with or without a login; a first visit follows the browser's) and the interface size.

items.title: Too many requests: wait and retry
items.text: When you go too fast, the game says how long to wait and tries again by itself instead of failing.

items.title: Keep me signed in
items.text: The sign-in form has Keep me signed in on this computer; untick it on a shared computer.

items.title: Your account in the settings
items.text: The page's Account settings change your name and email (with your password) and forget this computer.

items.title: Shiny lock
items.text: Set a Shiny lock in the Account settings: spending more than the amount you choose asks for your password first.

items.title: Auto play with stop rules
items.text: Magma Drop and Wormzer Roulette get AUTO, and every game's AUTO can stop after a number of rounds, when the run is down by an amount, or on a big win.

items.title: Take a bet back
items.text: A bet on Devil's Dice, Magma Derby or Balthazar's Ascent whose round hasn't started yet can be taken back, its Shiny paid back.

items.title: Map help in pages
items.text: The map's "?" opens help in short pages you can flip through.

items.title: Change Log: changed later
items.text: Entries that were changed or reversed later are marked so in the Change Log, and the Change Log has its own page.

items.title: Photo mode
items.text: Photo mode in the settings takes a picture of your yard to download, with filters and frames.

items.title: Replays of wild raids
items.text: A wild tribe's raid on your yard is recorded too: it has its row under Attacks on me, with what was lost, and a replay to watch.

items.title: More of the game in your language
items.text: The newer windows' texts are now in French, Spanish and Portuguese as well.

items.title: Incubator window with a queue just started
items.text: Opening an incubator the moment monsters were queued, before the first began hatching, could leave its window half drawn.

entries.headline: Emotes, alliance crests, champion skins and animated decorations, and a long list of fixes

items.title: Emotes
items.text: 52 emotes for the chat, 19 of them animated. Press the little devil-face button beside Say and pick one: it's sent at once, with whatever you had typed. Up to 5 in a line, and everyone sees them move. Free, and shown in the D.A.V.E. Club's new Emotes tab.

items.title: Design your own crest
items.text: An alliance's leader can now design a crest instead of picking one of the preset shields: Custom, first in the Edit form's shield grid, opens a designer with 6 shapes, 10 patterns, 24 emblems, 4 rims and 16 colours (or Random). The crest shows wherever your alliance's shield does: the alliance window, Browse, invites and the map. It's free, and picking a preset shield again puts that back.

items.title: Champion skins
items.text: Five new skins for every one of your champions: Molten, Void, Gilded, Bone and Venom. Pick a champion in the D.A.V.E. Club's Champions tab to see them all; each is 400 Shiny, yours for good, and you can switch between the looks you own at any time. Your champions wear them at home, in your attacks and for everyone who visits.

items.title: Animated decorations
items.text: 13 new decorations that move, in the build menu's Decorations, Animated: a Bubbling Cauldron, a Chained Imp that rattles his chain, a Lava Fountain, a Soul Lantern, a Hellfire Brazier, a Skull Totem, a Pendulum Blade, an Ember Geyser, the Eye of the Abyss, a Spit Roast, a Bat Weathervane, a Magma Waterwheel and a Tentacle Pit. 150 to 400 Shiny each.

items.title: The extra worker
items.text: "1 Extra Worker" can't be bought any more when a sacrifice has left you with four: it took the Shiny and gave nothing.

items.title: What your workers are doing
items.text: When every worker is busy, the message now names the job that ends soonest, how long it has left and what finishing it costs (or that it's free under 10 minutes). It used to send you to a store that doesn't sell workers.

items.title: Times read the same everywhere
items.text: Build, upgrade and training times use one style: the two largest units ("1d 5h", "2h 10m"), with seconds only under 10 minutes.

items.title: "Anyone home?"
items.text: Typing in the chat, the keyboard, the mouse wheel and up-and-down mouse movement now count as being there, so the away check doesn't interrupt you while you chat.

items.title: A bad connection doesn't stop the game
items.text: One failed connection check no longer stops the game with a reload. It tries again (after 3 and 6 seconds) and only gives up after three failures in a row.

items.title: Repairman and doctor
items.text: "Call the repairman!" and "Call the doctor!" have a close button.

items.title: Windows wait their turn
items.text: Messages that pop up by themselves wait until you close the Pit, an Arcade match, Hellgate Defense or the Quest Book, and the raid warning no longer hides behind them. Windows re-centre when the screen is resized or a phone is turned.

items.title: Please wait means wait
items.text: While the game shows "Please wait", a second click can't send the same thing again (power-ups, the Club's Save, takeovers, wave starts).

items.title: Healing costs what it should
items.text: "Heal All Monsters" no longer charges 10 Shiny for monster types that aren't hurt.

items.title: No Hatchery Overdrive where it's pointless
items.text: The Incubators' Speed up no longer offers Hatchery Overdrive: hatching takes a second here, so it only wasted Shiny.

items.title: Juicing asks first
items.text: Juicing monsters now asks you to confirm and names any champions in the batch. Select All leaves champions out (hold Shift to include them).

items.title: Training shows at once
items.text: Monsters trained in the Academy show their new health as soon as the training finishes, not after a reload.

items.title: Recycling keeps what's inside
items.text: Recycling a harvester banks what it holds. Recycling an Incubator banks the Magma of the monsters it was making and had queued. The Strongbox can't be recycled while it's unlocking.

items.title: Strongbox
items.text: The Strongbox checks its level before asking for Shiny.

items.title: Yesterday's dailies
items.text: Daily quests you finished but didn't collect before midnight (UTC) aren't lost any more: they stay in the Quest Book as "Yesterday:" for a day so you can still collect them.

items.title: No lost progress
items.text: Quest progress that fails to reach the server (a network blip) is kept and sent again.

items.title: Kits
items.text: Applying a kit sends the outpost's housed monsters home instead of deleting them, and the warning says how many. Underworld kits no longer charge for a Flinger that isn't built. If a kit was paid but not built (the line dropped), it tries again and then offers a Try again button. Kit slots that fail to load say so instead of looking empty, and Save says "Saving kit...".

items.title: Take over
items.text: A double click on "Use resources" can't pay twice, and errors read as words ("No answer from the server") with the cell checked again to show what really happened.

items.title: Wave starts
items.text: A double click on a wave start no longer uses up a try or loses the win.

items.title: Lost answers
items.text: If the Pit's answer to a bet is lost, it asks again (twice) instead of showing a refund for a bet that may have been played.

items.title: Send again
items.text: If a score doesn't reach the server, it tries again and then offers SEND AGAIN; a score that did arrive isn't counted twice.

items.title: Leaderboards
items.text: The boards show all 20 places, ten a page, and "Around you" when you're outside them. Balthazar's Flight has a This week board, for this week's course.

items.title: Co-op
items.text: In Co-op, a dropped connection counts as your partner leaving: you play on alone instead of losing the run.

items.title: Runs aren't lost
items.text: Every wave you clear is saved as you go. If the page is reloaded or closed mid-run, the run is recorded at the last wave cleared the next time you open Hellgate Defense (or Hellgate Defense 2). The browser also asks before you leave a run.

items.title: Replies
items.text: A reply the server refused or that didn't get through now says so, instead of vanishing.

items.title: Creating an alliance
items.text: A double click on Create no longer makes the alliance and then says the name is taken.

items.title: Appear offline
items.text: Players who appear offline no longer show as online in the alliance's Members tab and online count.

items.title: No-catapult runs
items.text: The no-catapult report is sent again if it doesn't arrive, and only counts once the server has it.

items.title: One day per date
items.text: Days that showed twice in this changelog are shown once.

items.title: Sign-ups
items.text: A name that's already taken no longer uses up your sign-ups: only accounts actually made count (five an hour from one connection), and if that's reached it says how long until the next.

items.title: Straight in
items.text: Registering logs you straight in: no more "Please login to continue".

items.title: Replies in a row
items.text: You can send up to three replies in a row before the other player answers (the reply box used to vanish after one).

items.title: Every wart counts
items.text: Picking lots of warts quickly (five workers in a Wart Bloom) all counts for the quests now; some picks were lost.

items.title: Later
items.text: An event's opening message can be put off with Later; start its first wave from the event's icon in the top bar when you're ready.

items.title: No stall on a full yard
items.text: An event's pieces now appear just outside a yard that has no room left, instead of never coming.

items.title: Results that get through
items.text: A won wave whose result didn't reach the server is sent again ("Saving the result..."), then offers Try again, so the win isn't lost.

items.title: Time to get ready
items.text: A raid that came due while you were away (in an outpost, the Gauntlet or someone's yard) now waits two minutes after you get home, and warns you again.

items.title: You'll hear it coming
items.text: Raids make a sound when they're announced and when they start, the countdown's last 30 seconds pulse, and its last five tick.

items.title: The Purist Trophy
items.text: Firing a catapult in the Gauntlet asks first while the Purist Trophy (all 13 gates without one) can still be won this month.

items.title: Muted stays muted
items.text: The sound and music buttons show that they're off after you switch yards (they always showed on).

items.title: Missing sounds
items.text: Candy Jars, Marilyn Monstroe and the vacuum make their sounds again, and Hellgate Defense's upgrades and explosions are no longer silent.

items.title: Music
items.text: With the next wave coming by itself, the fight's music plays on instead of starting again every wave.

items.title: Tidier Store
items.text: No Add Shiny button (Shiny can't be bought) and no old Social tab. The repair line says the real free time, and healing doesn't claim a free time it hasn't got.

items.title: Kits at once
items.text: A new outpost opens the kit list straight away, without the help page first.

items.title: Old words fixed
items.text: Lots of old text put right: Under Hall, Incubator, Strongbox, Compound and Monster Juicer where the old names were; the catapult's real ammunition; kits building instantly; tribe wins; the World Map's relocate tip; the invite button's tip (the Shiny you both get). Brag and Warn buttons are a plain OK, and the level-up message is the Inferno's own.

items.title: Build it
items.text: "You need a General Store" and "You need a Map Room" now have a Build it button that opens the Buildings window at it.

items.title: No dead invites
items.text: The "Invite friends to help speed up this upgrade" popup, whose button did nothing, is gone.

items.title: Your username works too
items.text: You can sign in with your username instead of your email, in any capitals.

items.title: No endless loading
items.text: If the language file doesn't load, the sign-in page tries again, then falls back to English, instead of waiting for ever.

items.title: Esc and Back
items.text: Esc cancels placing or moving a building, or closes the window on top. The browser's (or Android's) Back button does the same, and when nothing is open it asks "Leave the Inferno?" instead of closing the game.

items.title: Finish (Free)
items.text: A building job with the free time or less left has Finish (Free) right in its panel, instead of Speed up, the Store and Close Enough.

items.title: Collect everything
items.text: Click a resource's bar in the top bar to bank it from every harvester, or press C to bank them all.

items.title: Full screen
items.text: Zoom and chat now work in full screen.

items.title: Tower ranges
items.text: A tower's range ring follows it while you place or move it, and you can see towers' ranges when you hover them while scouting or attacking.

items.title: How long protection lasts
items.text: A protected yard's popup says how long its protection lasts ("Protected: 5h 12m"), and so does the message when you try to attack it. A damaged tribe yard says when it resets.

items.title: The 90% line
items.text: Every attack on an outpost or a tribe's yard shows the destruction bar with its 90% line, as Moloch's Gauntlet does.

items.title: Loading the Flinger
items.text: Shift-click or double-click "+" to fill the Flinger with one kind of monster; Shift-click "-" to take them all out. Press R to load it again as it was for your last fling.

items.title: Revenge
items.text: Attacks on you by other players have a Revenge button in the attack logs: it opens the map on the attacker's yard.

items.title: Outpost to outpost
items.text: Small arrows under the top bar's outposts counter go straight to the previous or next outpost, and the counter shows which one you're in ("12/40").

items.title: Idle workers
items.text: The Outposts list has an Idle column: workers with nothing to do in that outpost.

items.title: Relocating
items.text: Relocate's warning also counts the monsters housed in your outposts, and you type RELOCATE to confirm.

items.title: The Strongbox
items.text: While one monster unlocks, the others still show what they cost.

items.title: First steps
items.text: A new player is welcomed once and shown the Quest Book's first quest. The quest dock shows the Getting Started quests first until they're done, and there's a "Build a Flinger" step before "Fling your first monster".

items.title: Who's waiting
items.text: The Arcade's cabinets show how many players are waiting for a match.

items.title: After a run
items.text: The end screens have The Arcade and, after a linked match, Find another match, as well as Back home.

items.title: Click the header
items.text: Click the chat's header to open or close the chat (not only its small arrow).

items.title: Password twice
items.text: Signing up asks for your password a second time, in the same box, so a typo can't lock you out of a new account.

items.title: New messages below
items.text: Reading further up the chat, a "3 new ↓" button shows how many lines came in below (gold when one mentions you). Click it to jump down. The chat's fold arrow also sits further from its X.

items.title: A count on the button
items.text: The Alliances button on the top bar shows how many invites, join requests and new pins are waiting.

items.title: Invite by name
items.text: The Recruit tab has Invite by name, for a player who isn't among the suggestions.

items.title: More room
items.text: On a phone, the chat and the quest dock start folded the first time you play there. After that they stay the way you leave them.

items.title: Heal all
items.text: The Outposts list has Heal all when any outpost's defenders are still wounded from an attack, so you don't have to visit each one. Outposts under attack are left alone.

items.title: Portals say what they need
items.text: A portal you can't attack through yet names your nearest yard, how far it is, and how far that yard's Flinger reaches.

items.title: Remembers your settings
items.text: Each game keeps the bet you last used, Magma Drop keeps its risk, and the auto cash-out and auto bank boxes keep what you typed.

items.title: Undo, and plans for outposts
items.text: After Apply, a line says how many buildings moved, with Undo for a minute. Saving says when it's done, and a failed save no longer looks saved. Outposts can save and load plans too.

items.title: The quest dock's title
items.text: Click the quest dock's title bar to fold or open it.

items.title: Clearer steps
items.text: A seasonal event explains each step as it begins and shows how far along you are.

items.title: Fill the Compound
items.text: In the Incubator, Shift-click a monster to queue as many as there's room and Magma for. The monster's panel says how many that is.

items.title: Extra Housing ending
items.text: An hour before Extra Housing ends, you're told how much too little room the Compound will have. If monsters must go, they go one at a time from the kind you have most of (a lone champion no longer goes first), and you're told which.

items.title: The Juicer's total
items.text: The Juicer's total now matches what you get: the healthiest go first, and wounded monsters count for less.

items.title: Enter and clicking outside
items.text: Enter closes a message that only tells you something (never one that would spend or recycle). Clicking the dark area around the Change Log, Leaderboards, Attack Log, Quest Book, Who's Online, Outposts or Alliances window closes it.

items.title: Tower upgrade caution
items.text: The reminder that towers don't fire while upgrading shows once a session, not after every upgrade.

items.title: What's new
items.text: The Attack Log and Change Log buttons show how many attacks on you and new Change Log days you haven't seen yet. The Attack Log opens on Attacks on me when there are new ones.

items.title: End Attack asks
items.text: End Attack asks first while monsters and time are left, and in Moloch's Gauntlet it reminds you it uses an attempt.

items.title: Longer alliance chat
items.text: Alliance chat keeps its last 200 lines, and notices (joins, power-ups, pins) no longer push them out. The chat shows up to 120 lines.

items.title: Buildings not on a plan
items.text: Applying an older plan that doesn't place every building names them, and offers to keep them where they stand.

items.title: Quiet in the background
items.text: The page's settings have "Mute while this tab is hidden" (on by default). On phones and tablets the screen stays on during attacks, replays, Hellgate Defense, the Arcade and the Pit.

items.title: Times under the workers
items.text: Each busy worker shows the time left under it, and "Free" once the job can be finished for nothing: click it to finish. Clicking a busy worker opens the building it works on; an idle one opens the build menu.

items.title: Repair all is free
items.text: A damaged building's panel has Repair all, which starts every repair at once for free (it used to sell a Shiny repair).

items.title: What's waiting, and when it's full
items.text: Hovering a resource shows what your harvesters hold and when the storage will be full, and a full storage shows FULL on its bar.

items.title: Takeover price up front
items.text: A tribe yard's or outpost's popup says what taking it over would cost and whether you're short, or that you can't hold more outposts.

items.title: The Gauntlet is open
items.text: When Moloch's Gauntlet opens, your first visit home says so, until when in your own time, and how many gates are left, with a button to it.

items.title: Collect from the dock and the toast
items.text: Collecting in the quest dock says what you got, with the cha-ching. The "quest ready" toast shows the reward and has its own Collect.

items.title: When the next one is
items.text: Once today's reward is collected, its window says when the next one comes, in your own time.

items.title: The next wave
items.text: Winning an event wave offers to fight the next one right away.

items.title: Banned while playing
items.text: If an account is banned while it's playing, the game now says so and gives the reason (it said you had signed in somewhere else).

items.title: Clearer save errors
items.text: When a save fails, the message says so in words; the technical code is kept in small print for bug reports.

items.title: The tab's title
items.text: The browser tab's title shows how many mentions and messages are waiting, and when your yard is under attack.

items.title: One alliance at a time
items.text: Joining an alliance turns down your other pending invites, so they no longer wait in your list.

items.title: Removed from an alliance
items.text: A player removed from an alliance gets a letter saying who removed them, instead of finding out later.

items.title: New mail
items.text: A letter that arrives while you play is announced in a short line with an Open the mail button.

items.title: Go to a cell
items.text: Type coordinates such as 123,45 in the map's search and press Enter to go there.

items.title: More chat commands
items.text: /online opens Who's Online, /msg Name writes a letter to a player seen in chat, and /who Name finds them on the leaderboards. /help lists them all.

items.title: Zoom with the mouse wheel
items.text: The mouse wheel over your yard zooms in towards the pointer, up to three times. Turn it back to normal size, then turn it again to step out to the zoomed-out view.

items.title: Requirements you can click
items.text: A requirement you haven't met, underlined in red in the build or upgrade window ("Level 4 Under Hall"), opens that building's upgrade when clicked.

items.title: The Wart Bloom in your own time
items.text: While a Wart Bloom is on, a chip under the top bar says so and how long is left; click it for the end in your own time. Global chat now says how long it lasts instead of giving US Central time.

items.title: No more empty patches
items.text: When the server asked the map to slow down, the areas it refused stayed empty for a minute. They are now asked for again a few seconds later, and the limit is higher.

items.title: Under Hall and Resource Pods
items.text: Messages, quests and tips that still said Town Hall or Storage Silo now say Under Hall and Resource Pod, in every language. The Catapult's and the Incubator's descriptions were also brought up to date.

items.title: Where Shiny comes from
items.text: The not-enough-Shiny message now also lists sacrificing an idle worker to Moloch.

items.title: Letters that fit
items.text: A letter's box now stops at 580 characters, the most the server accepts, and counts down once 100 or fewer are left. A longer reply used to be refused and lost.

items.title: The Attack Log keeps its list
items.text: If the server asks the Attack Log to slow down, the list you had stays on screen and says it wasn't refreshed, instead of going blank. A report you open again shows at once.

items.title: Retry
items.text: If your alliance's Overview fails to load, it offers Retry instead of staying broken until you reload. A failed next page in the Outposts tab keeps the rows already shown, with Retry.

items.title: A ticking daily countdown
items.text: The daily quests' countdown in the Quest Book ticks every second, and the new day's quests come in as soon as it reaches zero.

items.title: When the gates rise again
items.text: The Gauntlet window gives the time the gates rise again in your own time, not "on the 1st" (in the Americas that's the evening before).

items.title: Chat daily
items.text: The daily "Chat in Global" quest now says lines count a minute apart and not repeated, like the book's chat quests.

items.title: No accidental new round
items.text: In Higher or Lower, START takes the place of CASH OUT, so a quick second tap no longer stakes a new round.

items.title: Fewer false alarms
items.text: An error message that popped up on a shaky connection for things the game does by itself in the background no longer appears. Errors still show for anything you do yourself.

items.title: Relocating on a bad line
items.text: If the answer to Relocate is lost, the game reloads to check where your yard is, instead of inviting you to relocate a second time.

items.title: Safer "can't be undone" questions
items.text: Recycling, stopping a build, cancelling an upgrade, relocating, sacrificing a worker, kicking, leaving and disbanding now ask the same way: a Keep button that only closes, and the action in red, which ignores clicks for its first moment so a double click can't go straight through.

items.title: Recycle says what you get
items.text: Recycle and stop-building questions name the building and its level, and say what comes back ("You get back: 12,000 Bone, 8,000 Coal").

items.title: Leave or Stay
items.text: Leaving or disbanding an alliance asks "Leave Hellions" / "Stay" instead of Yes / No.

items.title: Join requests with a message
items.text: Asking to join an alliance lets you add a few words for its leader. Leaders and officers see them with the request, along with your level, world, outposts and when you were last on.

items.title: The right keyboard
items.text: On phones the email field brings up the email keyboard, number fields a number pad, and the chat's Enter key says Send.

entries.headline: Saved logins, Who's Online, alliance tags and a night of fixes

items.title: VPNs and mobile data keep you signed in
items.text: A login now belongs to the browser it was made in instead of your internet connection, so switching a VPN on or off, or moving between Wi-Fi and mobile data, no longer signs you out. A login copied to another browser still doesn't work there.

items.title: Pick your name to sign in
items.text: The login page remembers up to 5 accounts. Clicking a name signs you straight in without the password, for 14 days after you last played on that account. After that, or if you remove the name with its x, the password is asked for again.

items.title: Playing somewhere else?
items.text: Signing in while your account is already playing on another device or tab now asks first. Play here signs the other one out (it's told why); No leaves it playing and you stay on the login page. Reloading the same tab, or opening the game again after closing it, asks nothing.

items.title: A new password signs out everywhere
items.text: Changing your password ends every saved login and game on every device.

items.title: Reload keeps your account
items.text: Reloading a tab signs back in as the account that tab was playing, even if another tab in the same browser has since switched to a different account.

items.title: Messages over open windows
items.text: A message, a "Please wait" or a second window opened over the Leaderboards, the Attack Log, the Brimstone Pit or the Gauntlet is drawn properly again where it covers the window.

items.title: Something in the Ashes
items.text: A new quest in the Battles chapter. Something has been watching you fight: win battle after battle, and in time it may decide to fight at your side.

items.title: The daily countdown counts
items.text: The daily quests' countdown keeps counting down while the Quest Book is open.

items.title: Seeds change between games
items.text: Changing your seeds now waits until the Bone Pile, Higher or Lower, Undertaker's Offer or Cinderjack game you have open is finished.

items.title: Every speed-up counts
items.text: Speeding up an alliance power-up from two places at once (or two members at the same moment) now takes off every hour that was paid for.

items.title: Asked on the map too
items.text: Signing in on another device while you are on the world map or in an attack now asks first, as it does while you're in your yard (it signed the other one out without asking after 2 minutes away from the yard).

items.title: No moving away mid-attack
items.text: Moving your yard onto an outpost, to a random place or to an alliance member's outpost now waits until an attack on your yard is over, as relocating already did.

items.title: Who's Online?
items.text: A small Who's Online? button on the left of the chat bar lists everyone online now (active in the last 5 minutes) and everyone on in the last day, most recent first, with their alliance tags. A player who closes the game shows as recently online from then. Appear offline, at the list's top right, keeps you off everyone else's list and greys your dot in chat until you turn it back.

items.title: Alliance tags and online dots
items.text: Names in chat show the player's alliance tag in brackets instead of their yard level, coloured by how your alliance stands with theirs: blue for your own, green for friendly, red for hostile, gold for the rest. Players without an alliance have no tag. A green dot before the name means they're online, grey means they aren't.

items.title: Rename your alliance, set its tag
items.text: Leaders can now rename their alliance and set its chat tag (1 to 5 letters or numbers) from Edit on the Overview tab. Until a leader sets one, the tag is the first 3 letters of the alliance's name. A rename is announced in alliance chat.

items.title: One leader at a time
items.text: Handing over the lead, or making an officer, at the same moment from two places can no longer leave an alliance with two leaders.

items.title: A better name menu
items.text: Clicking a name in the chat or in Who's Online opens its menu right next to the mouse. It now shows the player's tag and whether they're online, and adds Mention in chat, Copy name and, for alliance leaders and officers, Invite to my alliance.

items.title: Alliance chat always opens
items.text: If the alliance's chat history can't be loaded, the Alliance tab still opens and new lines still arrive, and one line the game can't show no longer hides every line after it.

items.title: Fairer chat
items.text: Banned accounts can no longer post, the flood limit counts per player instead of per connection, and a game that was signed out can't go on chatting. A muted player's board pins are no longer announced in alliance chat.

items.title: A wider chat box
items.text: The chat box is a little wider, and each message's time ("5m", "2h") now shows in full at the right instead of being hidden under the scroll bar.

items.title: Purchases need the Shiny
items.text: Store items and protection now need enough Shiny for their price: with too little, the purchase is refused instead of going through. Buying several of something whose price rises charges the price of each one, and an outpost's store charges what it shows.

items.title: Takeovers are paid for
items.text: Taking over an outpost or a yard on the map always needs its price, in Shiny or in resources.

items.title: Range checked everywhere
